1417	## 5. Durable custody and failure protocol
1418	
1419	Default `opensip`/`analyze` is DURABLE_AUTHORITATIVE under CD-RT-5. The host
1420	reports retention origin DEFAULTED and durable-unbounded posture before first
1421	write; the command's documented effect is admission of the project marker and
1422	private registry/store, followed by an authoritative Run. No implicit policy
1423	file is written. Explicit retention overrides have independent byte/time/count
1424	bounds with provenance; failure to satisfy an authoritative request never
1425	silently demotes it to ephemeral. `--ephemeral` is explicitly non-authoritative,
1426	uses temporary custody, mints no authoritative commit receipt and cannot satisfy
1427	baseline adoption, repair or authoritative replay prerequisites.
1428	
1429	The storage-root admission still applies the inherited sync, backup and private
1430	custody classifications separately. A detected backup-managed root requires an
1431	explicit storage-policy choice before the first source-derived write (TM V17):
1432	select another admitted root, choose explicit ephemeral mode, or acknowledge
1433	backup custody for this invocation with `--allow-backup-custody` (or the
1434	corresponding already-admitted host storage-policy record). CI never prompts;
1435	without that explicit choice it refuses REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED with detail
1436	`storage.backup-choice-required`, before creating evidence. The acknowledgement
1437	is retained as operational custody metadata; it does not alter semantic Run
1438	identity or silently write a policy file. UNKNOWN backup status is disclosed as
1439	unknown, never as not-backed-up. Purge never claims deletion of external copies.
1440	Sync/upload roots and group/ACL exposure retain their separate admission rules;
1441	a backup acknowledgement is not a network-export or shared-storage grant.
1442	
1443	Exactly one per-project writer holds the lifecycle lease/fence through source
1444	admission, evaluation and atomic commit. Read-only clients use a consistent
1445	committed ledger snapshot and never wait while holding a lock needed by the
1446	writer. Global trust admission and revocation use the security contract's lock
1447	order. SQLite WAL, transaction settings, fsync/atomic-rename carrier and crash
1448	reconciliation retain the reviewed lifecycle carrier's native obligations;
1449	the reference model here tests the semantic transition, not OS durability.
1450	
1451	Commit order:
1452	
1453	1. Validate closure and independently replay proof; compute all final IDs.
1454	2. Write immutable blobs and descriptors to private temporary files, verify
1455	   digest/length, fsync files, atomically publish under digest, fsync directories.
1456	3. In one synchronous ledger transaction insert Run manifest, object references,
1457	   retained availability generation, baseline/other authorized pins and a commit
1458	   receipt with ExecutionId, namespace, monotonic sequence, inventory digest,
1459	   signer and immutable assurance; commit and satisfy the carrier's barriers.
1460	4. Only then acknowledge commitment. Required rendering/delivery is later and
1461	   cannot rewrite the Run. Receipt signing is operational custody evidence and
1462	   excluded from semantic IDs; the receipt authenticates RunId and inventory.
1463	
1464	A failure before step 3 publishes no authoritative Run. Orphan blobs are
1465	unreferenced and eligible for GC after reconciliation. A crash after ledger
1466	commit but before acknowledgement is `durability-undetermined` to the caller,
1467	exit 4, with an ExecutionId for read-only recovery. Recovery checks the ledger
1468	and actual objects; it returns committed or failed, never repeats a repository
1469	mutation. Duplicate retry can share a Run but has a separate attempt receipt.
1470	An acknowledged Run with missing/corrupt objects becomes partially available or
1471	corrupt; the host does not pretend it was never sealed.
1472	
1473	Sealed assurance is immutable: verified means exact identity+proof checks at
1474	seal; verifiable also commits the verification closure; replayable also commits
1475	all exact admitted producer executables and source/input closure. The default
1476	authoritative profile requires replayable retention at seal. Current
1477	availability is a separate monotonic-generation record: retained, partial,
1478	expired, purged, corrupt or unavailable, with exact missing references and
1479	cause. Availability may improve through verified restoration or regeneration;
1480	sealed assurance and historical verdict never change. A query reports both.
1481	
1482	Retention roots include every live Run's required closure, active baseline,
1483	authorized repair prerequisite and backup/export operation pin. Automatic
1484	expiry respects these pins and all independent policy bounds; it refuses a
1485	new durable admission if the required closure cannot be retained within bounds.
1486	A direct purge of a pinned Run refuses unless the explicit destructive purge
1487	also revokes the named pins after disclosing consequences. That refusal has a
1488	registered public projection and this contract does not restate it: the
1489	foundation-owned detail `evidence.pinned` projects as `request-rejected`,
1490	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, exit 2, carrying the closed
1491	`common.schema.json#/$defs/PinnedPurgeDisclosure` — the RunId, the complete
1492	current `activePins` inventory sorted uniquely by `pinId`, and the three ordered
1493	consequences `named-pins-revoked`,
1494	`dependent-evidence-replay-unavailable`, `sealed-history-retained` — exactly as
1495	**workflows-and-surfaces §12** specifies. No pin is omitted, truncated or
1496	aggregated into a count. Neither that disclosure nor any flag confers authority:
1497	a later destructive attempt still requires the explicit lifecycle authorization
1498	and disclosure of its then-current complete pin set, and a changed pin inventory
1499	requires renewed disclosure before destruction. Purge retains the
1500	minimal sealed manifest, provenance and tombstone but deletes unshared evidence
1501	bytes by reachability GC; shared bytes survive until the final reference is
1502	removed. Purged is not deleted-history. The user may separately destroy the
1503	whole project store/marker under lifecycle authorization; no indefinite privacy
1504	claim is made for backups or exports already outside that store.
1505	
1506	A retention decision never changes a fact, Coverage, finding or Run identity.
1507	It never turns expired evidence into `no match`. Query of retained manifest is
1508	allowed after purge and states evidence unavailable. Query requiring actual
1509	proof, comparison baseline or repair input refuses with
1510	REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED and `evidence.{expired,purged,missing,corrupt}`
1511	before evaluation (exit 2); inability during a selected operation is HOST.IO_FAILURE
1512	with evidence detail (exit 4). Successfully admitted partial native inputs may
1513	instead produce an indeterminate Run (exit 3) under the native and D9 contracts.
1514	These are different event positions, not interchangeable error spellings.
1515	
1516	Backup/export holds a read snapshot plus short-lived object pins, writes a
1517	bounded relative-path inventory, hashes and verifies every object, then seals
1518	the bundle. Import checks path traversal, symlinks, sizes, duplicate paths,
1519	cryptographic identities and all referenced schemas before publishing anything.
1520	Source provenance/authenticity is reported separately from hash integrity.
1521	Trust floors, current authorization and local custody receipts are never
1522	restored backwards from an evidence backup. Portable baseline details are in
1523	the workflow contract. An import cannot silently claim a remote Run was locally
1524	evaluated: its imported-custody receipt names origin and local verification.
1525	
1526	## 6. Required implementation conformance
1527	
1528	Reference checks cover exact numeric and canonical encodings, wrong-source and
1529	wrong-Plan joins, identity changes for each semantic input, operational identity
1530	exclusion, universal negatives under incomplete resolution, proof tampering,
1531	retention/purge invariance and crash acknowledgement states. They additionally
1532	assert the digest law mechanically: that every 64-hex field carries a registered
1533	representation, that each new closed record reproduces an independently computed
1534	canonical digest vector and moves under every single-field mutation, and that a
1535	complete Run with a non-empty native context set closes while an altered frame, a
1536	missing preimage, a wrong preimage, an unregistered H domain, a raw payload
1537	offered as an H identity and a hidden input each refuse with a typed cause. They
1538	also assert that a fully re-framed and re-keyed Run built around a context the
1539	native boundary refuses — contradicting honored options, a compiler or runtime
1540	digest outside the tool closure, an incomplete stdlib inventory, a component
1541	digest that is not the retained tree's, a compiler version not from the manifest,
1542	a universe contradicting its context, or a config graph or lockfile path outside
1543	the snapshot — is refused with that boundary's own typed refusal string. They
1544	exercise a complete Rust universe/fact/Coverage Run alongside the TypeScript one,
1545	with the nested dependency, features, config-projection and prepared-output
1546	records retained and joined; and they separate cache key construction from cache
1547	hit admission, showing that a key needs no bytes while a hit needs the Run's whole
1548	closure. Their source pins
1549	and independent review are part of D-372. They do not qualify a native carrier.
1550	
1551	Before shipping, the exact implementation must additionally demonstrate:
1552	all supported platform fsync/SQLite/process-death cases; concurrent readers and
1553	writers plus trust revocation; independent replay across machines; missing,
1554	corrupt, stale and wrong-tenant closure rejection; hostile archive import; GC
1555	with shared references; backup restoration preserving trust floors; and public
1556	D9/CLI/JSON/SARIF/HTML/agent parity. Those are implementation acceptance criteria
1557	under existing G gates, not unresolved design alternatives.
1558	
1559	### Reference lifecycle joins
1560	
1561	The reference store instantiates closed commit-receipt and availability records.
1562	An availability transition increments generation and never rewrites a sealed Run
1563	or its original assurance. Read-only `recover(ExecutionId)` inspects the committed
1564	receipt after a lost acknowledgement and never repeats effects. Verified restoration
1565	requires the same complete identity closure and replay result before availability
1566	returns to retained; a regeneration mismatch refuses. Physical fsync, authenticated
1567	receipt signing, shared-blob deletion and OS crash recovery remain implementation
1568	qualification obligations; the reference transitions do not claim to execute them.
1569	
1570	The security chapter's three lease modes refine the inherited single-writer rule:
1571	immutable readers coexist with the append writer; exclusive migration/purge acquires
1572	the writer lease and reader exclusion. No second writer is permitted.
1573	
1574	At Run closure, every Plan-selected import re-admits its retained canonical SourceCorrespondence. An exact-snapshot import must name the Plan snapshot. VCS-revision imports require a retained, canonical admitted SourceMappingV1 to that snapshot, with inventory-matching source digests and the current clean revision; an unmapped/stale intake artifact may remain available for inspection but cannot be selected as an analyzed Plan input. Intake storage does not establish this source join. The authenticated importer/evaluator still owns payload-schema, observation-scope and polarity admission; rehashing an opaque import is insufficient. The reference closure reuses the same workflow import/mapping schema admission functions so the source law has one implementation.
1575	
1576	The semantic grant's `prepare-code` operation is present exactly when it projects trusted-repository-code preparation principals. Their provenance comes from consumed admitted host-prepared inputs; no test-runner operation or principal is added. Verification/replay checks these immutable bindings without reusing expired operational grants.
1577	
1578	The expected VCS build context is explicit, never inferred from the imported claim. The host may select one analysis-spec parameter whose schemaDigest is the raw SHA-256 of `foundation/import-source-context.schema.json` and whose payloadDigest binds canonical ImportSourceContextV1 `{schemaVersion:1, declaredBuildIds:[...]}`. These expected labels come from the separately admitted analysis request/build configuration; the importer cannot nominate its own expected labels. No parameter means an empty set; more than one is refused. Labels are declarations, not proof: source mapping remains mandatory. Run closure reconstructs workflow §4's binding from this retained parameter and the snapshot's VCS observation, then applies the same staleness function (both dirty flags, revision, expected build label and admitted mapping). A label not in the expected set is wrong-build and cannot become a Plan-selected import. The schema bytes and payload are retained with the Plan parameters for independent replay.
1579	
1580	Snapshot capture consumes the same admitted boundary inventory as native discovery. The host obtains it from successful security discovery, passes it unchanged to native discovery/membership and the shared scope descriptor, and removes nested-repository, nested-project and directory-custody-excluded paths before opening or hashing snapshot source bytes. The remaining paths are only capture candidates: per-file custody, safe handles and exact hashing still precede source admission. Boundary exclusion anchors enter the Plan's scope descriptor and their operational provenance is retained beside it. The host reference join admits one inventory; caller-supplied alternative boundary lists or substituted marker sets are refused. Discovery's dependency-tree pruning is an analysis-unit rule; explicitly required native dependency read-set bytes require separate custody/closure admission and cannot cross a nested authority boundary.
1581	
1582	Every Plan with selected import2 inputs also requires read-import in its semantic grant. This includes imported-inert preparation. Close_run enforces this operation/input join as well as prepare-code/principal equality; the later consuming-Plan admission separately validates the actual preparedResolution provenance.
1583	
1584	
1585	The reference closure entry point reports a missing promised object/blob as EvidenceUnavailable carrying the closed operational-failed/HOST.IO_FAILURE/host-io termination with evidence.missing and the missing reference. It never emits a bare lookup error or turns missing witness bytes into a false predicate or admission rejection. This models the host's retained-byte/custody observation boundary. Untrusted malformed records still receive exact schema/identity admission refusal; an inventory of available retained bytes does not authorize rewriting the assurance of a sealed Run.

62	## 1. Invocation, step, attempt, Run (AR-08)
63	
64	An invocation is one host request. Its operational identity is `RequestId`, minted
65	before admission and retained for refusal as well as success. The invocation is an
66	ordered acyclic list of at most **64 steps**; `StepId` is the zero-based position.
67	Each admitted attempt of a step receives a fresh `ExecutionId`; a step has at most
68	**3 attempts**. Only `analysis` and `verify` steps seal or link a content-derived
69	`run2`. `comparison`, `query`, `render`, `import`, `repair-preview`, `repair-apply`,
70	`test-execution`, `native-preparation`, `mutation`, `export-delivery` and `doctor` are operational steps
71	that never mint a Run. Schema: `invocation-record.schema.json`.
72	
73	**Step DAG versus derivation DAG.** The step list is the operational workflow. Each
74	analysis/verify *attempt* owns exactly one derivation DAG (`exec-plan2`, at most
75	**1024 stages**) recorded in the attempt's `derivation` binding
76	(`planId`, `executionPlanId`, `stageCount`, `stagesCompleted`, `firstFailedStage`).
77	A step never depends on a stage and a stage never references a step. A retry on
78	identical admitted inputs may bind the same `exec-plan2` and the same Run; attempts
79	remain separately auditable.
80	
81	**Dependencies.** `dependsOn` names lower StepIds only (a forward or self reference is
82	`WORKFLOW.DEPENDENCY_CYCLE`, request-rejected). `requirement` is `required` or
83	`optional`; a required step may not depend on an optional step
84	(`WORKFLOW.REQUIRED_DEPENDS_ON_OPTIONAL`). `dependencyGate` is `completed` (every
85	dependency completed) or `terminal` (every dependency reached any terminal outcome;
86	lawful only for `render`/`export-delivery`, which project whatever happened). A
87	step whose gate is unmet is `skipped` with a typed `skipReason`. Step outcomes are
88	closed: `completed`, `rejected`, `failed`, `skipped`, `cancelled`, `abandoned`
89	(crash recovery only).
90	
91	**Retries.** `retryPolicy=idempotent-retry` is lawful only for `analysis`, `verify`,
92	`query`, `render`, `doctor` and `export-delivery`, only for `faultCause=ledger-busy`,
93	and within the 3-attempt budget; exhausting it is `LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT` (4) with
94	detail `WORKFLOW.RETRY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`. `host-io` and every other fault are never
95	retried. `mutation`, `import`, `repair-preview`, `repair-apply`, `comparison`, `native-preparation` and `test-execution`
96	carry `retryPolicy=none` by schema; a spec violating this is refused.
97	
98	**Mutation idempotence and recovery.** Generic `mutation` steps use the bare
99	64-hex `H("workflow.mutation-intent", MutationReplayScopeV1)`. The closed retained
100	scope is exactly `{schemaVersion:1,requestId,stepId,projectId,operation}`, with
101	`operation` equal to `MutationParams.mutationClass`. This explicitly succeeds the
102	former undefined `{operation,projectId,effect preimage}` description. The key is
103	operational and scoped to one host-minted request and admitted immutable step;
104	different fresh requests never deduplicate each other's generic mutations.
105	`sourceStep` resolves inside that same retained invocation, whose admitted
106	parameters and completed dependency results are immutable. Before lookup or
107	replay the host validates the scope and full params, recomputes the key and
108	requires the retained invocation/project/step/operation binding; a caller cannot
109	nominate another invocation's scope or change effect inputs under an old key.
110	Receipt lookup is never an effect-authorization mechanism. A same-scope COMPLETED
111	receipt permits delivery replay with no second effect. Failure, unknown state or
112	incomplete execution requires the operation's existing recovery law, not blind
113	re-execution. Recovery started in a new request retains its own operational scope
114	and the explicit original journal/intent links required by §§6/12.
115	
116	**What a step's required receipt carries is published, not inferred.**
117	`MutationReceiptV1` **requires** both `operation` and `idempotencyKey`, and
118	`ImportResult` and `NativePreparationResult` both **require** a `receiptId`. The
119	owning domain for those branches is `workflow.mutation-receipt` — the **mutation**
120	receipt domain, not the only `receipt2:` one, since §10 also lists
121	`workflow.verification-link`. So an import step and a native-preparation step each
122	already owe a receipt carrying **both** required fields, and what was missing was
123	the binding for each. The operation binding is published as
124	`repair.schema.json#/x-opensip-mutation-operation-map/byStepKindReceiptOperation`,
125	beside the enum, and it is a deterministic function of the **step kind**:
126	
127	| Step kind | Receipt operation | Also carried in a request field? |
128	|---|---|---|
129	| `mutation` | the command's row in `byCommandGenericMutationStep` | yes — `MutationParams.mutationClass`, equal to `MutationReplayScopeV1.operation` |
130	| `repair-apply` | `repair-apply` | no — dedicated step, refused in both generic fields |
131	| `import` | `import` | no — `ImportParams`; §4's import receipt |
132	| `native-preparation` | `native-preparation` | no — `NativePreparationParams`; native §14's execution receipt |
133	
134	Because the binding is by **step kind and not by request class**, the `import`
135	step of the `analyze` command carries the same operation as the `import`
136	command's. That is also a worked case of **one operation emitted by two
137	commands**, which is why this map is *not* an inverse map and must not be read
138	backwards. A command with none of these four step kinds mints no operation.
139	
140	**The idempotency key is bound too, and sharing a recipe is not sharing replay
141	authority.** `receiptIdempotencyKeyByStepKind` publishes, per step kind, the exact
142	deterministic preimage and the *lookup meaning* separately:
143	
144	| Step kind | Key | Lookup meaning |
145	|---|---|---|
146	| `mutation` | `H("workflow.mutation-intent", MutationReplayScopeV1)` | equal COMPLETED receipt permits delivery replay with no second effect |
147	| `repair-apply` | raw SHA-256 of `C({operation, projectId, repairPlanId, baseSnapshotId})` | equal completed key performs no second effect |
148	| `import` | the same H over the closed scope with `operation: "import"` | **delivery only**, within the same retained invocation; never a cross-request dedupe |
149	| `native-preparation` | the same H with `operation: "native-preparation"` | **not replay**: it identifies that step's receipt and authorizes nothing |
150	
151	No new H domain, record or authority is introduced: `MutationReplayScopeV1.operation`
152	**already admits** both tokens — they are two of the 23 — which is a further reason
153	that domain stays wider than the current generic emitters. The user-supplied import
154	path is deliberately **not** in the preimage, because §4 keeps it out of identity
155	entirely. The receipt key is operational and already contains `RequestId`.
156	`ExecutionId` stays out because this key is scoped to one admitted invocation and
157	step; each attempt keeps its separate `ExecutionId`. These immutable bindings
158	grant no execution or retry authority.
159	
160	**The three non-generic kinds are still not generic replay.** They carry their own
161	params rather than `MutationParams`, are not generic `mutation` steps, and carry
162	`retryPolicy=none` by schema. Import custody, mandatory source correspondence and
163	the staleness disposition are unchanged and re-checked — a receipt substitutes for
164	none of them. A fresh native preparation is a **new explicit authorized execution**
165	under its own `AuthorizedExecutionV2` and grant set with **no automatic retry**; a
166	completed receipt never suppresses one, and this binding grants no permission the
167	security unit does not already admit.
168	
169	Across these step kinds, **four** commands do not share their operation's name,
170	so the operation cannot be derived by name matching. Three use generic mutation steps:
171	`baseline-upgrade` → `baseline-upgrade-apply` (the operation names the apply
172	half; the analysis half mints a Run, not a mutation), `policy-init` →
173	`policy-write` and `waive` → `waiver-change` (both are effect classes covering
174	more than the one command spelling). The fourth is the execution-class
175	`native-prepare` → `native-preparation`, whose operation is carried by its own
176	step kind; it is published with the other three because counting only the
177	mutation-class commands would leave one command's operation still underivable.
178	The published set is held **equal** to the commands whose name is not itself a
179	`MutationOperation` member, so a later rename cannot be added to the vocabulary
180	without appearing here. Two further facts are disclosed rather than tidied away:
181	`repair-apply` is bound by its own step kind, and being in the map does **not**
182	make it admissible in either generic position — both still refuse it by schema;
183	and `config-write` is the one `MutationOperation` member that **no step kind binds
184	and no command in this inventory emits**, which is stated rather than removed or
185	given an invented command, and which stays admissible in the generic field because
186	narrowing a generic domain to today's emitters would remove a value no finding
187	asked to remove. Publishing the map adds no command, no operation, no receipt and
188	no accepted request. What the reference model in this kit does **not** do is emit
189	an import or native-preparation receipt; that is a stated qualification limit of
190	the reference evidence and is deliberately distinct from the design law above.
191	
192	Repair apply is the explicit content-derived exception: it is a dedicated
193	`repair-apply` step, excluded from generic MutationParams. It uses the raw SHA-256 of
194	canonical `{operation:"repair-apply",projectId,repairPlanId,baseSnapshotId}` as its
195	idempotency key. An equal completed key performs no second effect. The original
196	receipt is immutable; a replay delivery produces a separately identified receipt
197	with the new request/attempt binding and `replayed=true`. Mutation receipts use
198	`receipt2:` plus `H('workflow.mutation-receipt', receiptWithoutReceiptId)` and remain
199	retained when an effect or later verification fails. Read-only recovery inspection
200	is distinct from separately authorized recovery writes (§6).
201	
202	**Audit gate ownership.** An analysis step declares `verdictGate=self|delegated`.
203	`self` applies its Run verdict. `delegated` requires authoritative analysis and a
204	consuming comparison step: a completed failing Run then contributes operational
205	success with its RunId, while the comparison owns the regression gate. This lets
206	inherited findings remain visible without failing the PR. Missing required Coverage
207	still contributes indeterminate; delegation cannot hide an incomplete analysis.
208	The comparison result is a distinct closed `ComparisonStepResult`, never a Run.
209	
210	**Cancellation.** A signal is recorded with the phase at which it arrived.
211	*before-settle* (some required step not yet terminal): remaining steps are
212	`cancelled`, the aggregate is `interrupted` (130), and a Run committed by an earlier
213	step is named in the termination's `runId`. *after-settle* (every required step
214	already terminal): the aggregate is **not reclassified**; the settled class stands.
215	Per kind: an analysis attempt aborts and leaves no Run; an import discards its
216	staged bytes; a repair-apply honours cancellation only before `APPLYING`, and during
217	the bounded rename loop the journal, not the signal, decides (§6).
218	
219	**Aggregate termination (D9 ordering preserved).** Over required steps only:
220	`operational-failed` > `request-rejected` > `policy-failed` > `indeterminate` >
221	`success`. An optional step's rejection or failure never changes the aggregate.
222	Policy fail dominates indeterminate across steps exactly as inside one Run, and a
223	required operational fault dominates a committed failing Run (its `runId` is still
224	carried). Exit code derives from class by the fixed table only. Ties retain the first
225	termination carrying domain detail in step order, or the first termination when
226	none carries detail, so a useful comparison remedy is preserved.
227	
228	**Ephemeral analysis.** `--ephemeral` produces the second member of the closed
229	`AnalysisResult` union: `authority=ephemeral`, `durability=not-required`, no `runId`,
230	no receipt, only semantic `planId`/`evidenceId` so the result can be cited. It cannot
231	satisfy baseline adoption, repair preview/apply, verify or authoritative replay
232	(`WORKFLOW.EPHEMERAL_CANNOT_SUPPLY_AUTHORITY`, `REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE`, exit 2). A
233	failing ephemeral verdict terminates `policy-failed` with `authority=ephemeral`
234	instead of a `runId`; the branch contract admits exactly one of the two.
235	
236	**Default invocation.** `opensip` with no arguments is discovery then one durable
237	authoritative analysis (steps `analysis`, `render`). Retention is DEFAULTED
238	durable-unbounded (CD-RT-5), disclosed with the storage root before first write.
239	No policy file is written implicitly.

243	## 2. Portable baseline and runnable prior detector (AR-10)
244	
245	`BaselineArtifactV1` lives in the repository as tracked intent
246	(`opensip.baseline.json`). `baselineId = H('workflow.baseline', descriptor)`. The
247	descriptor pins: origin ProjectId, source `snapshot2`, the **authoritative** `run2`
248	and `plan2` (an ephemeral result is refused: `BASELINE.SOURCE_EPHEMERAL`), the
249	fingerprint recipe (`finding-fingerprint`, major ≥ 2), every contributing detector's
250	`closure2` with semantics major, the complete **pivot closure** (detector executable,
251	evaluator, toolchain/stdlib, schema set; each a `closure2` with manifest digest,
252	protocol major and platform), the evaluation context digests, the **embedded**
253	policy/scope/waiver documents whose digests equal those context digests, rule
254	coverage, and sorted unique entries. Custody (outside identity) carries host release,
255	export time, `retentionPins` (the Run and every pivot closure) and an optional signed
256	`closureBundle` reference.
257	
258	**Fresh CI.** Comparison never reads the origin machine's store. A fresh host admits
259	the artifact by recomputing `baselineId`, checking schema major, recipe major,
260	sortedness, context-document digests and project correspondence (same ProjectId, or
261	explicit `--accept-origin`, else `BASELINE.PROJECT_UNMAPPED` and no comparison). It
262	resolves each pivot closure from (a) a retained generation, (b) an installed signed
263	release with the same `closure2`, or (c) the signed closure bundle; all under
264	**current trust**. A closure that is missing (`pivot-detector-unavailable`), revoked
265	(`pivot-closure-revoked`) or incompatible with the host's protocol majors/platform
266	(`pivot-closure-incompatible`) makes E0 unavailable; a revoked closure is never
267	executed, whatever bytes are present.
268	
269	**Detector semantics.** Semantics can change within a major, so two-way comparison
270	is lawful only when the closures are identical (`identical-closure`) or the current
271	detector's signed manifest lists the baseline `closure2` as exactly semantically
272	compatible at the same major (`declared-compatible`). Otherwise the baseline detector
273	must run over current source (`three-way-pivot`, an authoritative pivot analysis step
274	planned before the primary one) or the detector's entries are `INDETERMINATE`.
275	Fingerprint dual emission (`legacyFingerprint`) migrates identity only and never
276	supplies the prior algorithm. Adoption pins the Run and the pivot closures as
277	retention roots; loss of a pin is disclosed as partial availability and yields typed
278	indeterminacy, never a silent two-way fallback. `baseline-upgrade` re-adopts under the
279	current detector explicitly and is a mutation with its own receipt.

283	## 3. Multi-axis comparison (AR-11)
284	
285	`ComparisonResultV1` (`comparison2:` = `H('workflow.comparison', descriptor)`)
286	attributes every fingerprint to the **first** axis at which it changes along a fixed
287	counterfactual chain evaluated over *current* source:
288	
289	| Pivot | Facts from | Policy | Scope | Waivers |
290	|---|---|---|---|---|
291	| B | baseline artifact entries | prior | prior | prior |
292	| E0 | prior detector closure over current source | prior | prior | prior |
293	| E1 | current detector | prior | prior | prior |
294	| E2 | current detector | current | prior | prior |
295	| E3 | current detector | current | current | prior |
296	| E4 | current Run | current | current | current |
297	
298	Axis order is code (B→E0), detection (E0→E1), policy (E1→E2), scope (E2→E3),
299	waiver (E3→E4, by waived status). E1–E3 are pure re-evaluations of retained current
300	facts under the baseline's embedded documents. They are available only when their
301	results were actually bound; an unchanged axis is `not-needed`, and a required
302	unbound re-evaluation is `unavailable` with typed indeterminacy. E0 is
303	`not-needed` when the detector is unchanged or declared compatible, `available`
304	when the pivot ran, `unavailable` otherwise. Classifications are `UNCHANGED`,
305	`CODE-NET-NEW`, `CODE-FIXED`, `DETECTION-DELTA`, `POLICY-DELTA`, `SCOPE-DELTA`,
306	`WAIVER-DELTA`, `EVIDENCE-DELTA`, `INDETERMINATE`; each entry also records
307	`presence` at every pivot and `subsequentDeltas` (later axes at which it changed
308	again). Deleting a waiver while adding a bug therefore yields one `WAIVER-DELTA` and
309	one `CODE-NET-NEW`; a bug introduced and simultaneously hidden by disabling the rule
310	is `CODE-NET-NEW` with `subsequentDeltas=[policy]`.
311	
312	**Detector union.** Comparison covers the union of baseline and current detectors.
313	Added detectors set E0 false. Removed detectors require the actual current-trusted
314	prior detector pivot and set E1–E4 false; E0 must never be substituted with B.
315	Consequently a new bug hidden by removing its detector remains CODE-NET-NEW and
316	can gate. Missing prior execution is indeterminate, including detector removal.
317	
318	**Evidence axis.** Compare the exact bound `import2` identity sets per kind, with
319	payload/correspondence/scope/observation digests retained in each BoundImport.
320	Replacing an artifact with another of the same kind is still an evidence change
321	(`evidence-content-changed`). For a rule with declared `evidenceUse`: if required evidence is
322	absent on the current side the entry is `INDETERMINATE`
323	(`required-evidence-unavailable`) and the rule's coverage is unsatisfied; if
324	availability changed and the rule gates on either side, attribution is
325	`INDETERMINATE` (`evidence-availability-changed`); only for a non-gating rule may a
326	presence change be `EVIDENCE-DELTA`. Required evidence loss can never disappear as a
327	non-gating delta.
328	
329	**Audit profiles select gate semantics explicitly** (schema `AuditProfile`):
330	
331	| Profile | Gates CODE-NET-NEW | Gates newly live via policy/scope/waiver | Gates all current live | New waiver suppresses net-new | Rule gating under |
332	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
333	| `code-regression` (default for `audit`) | yes | no | no | no | baseline or current |
334	| `policy-change` | yes | yes | no | no | baseline or current |
335	| `full-current` | yes | yes | yes | yes | current only |
336	| `report-only` | no | no | no | yes | current only |
337	
338	A `CODE-NET-NEW` entry that is not live in current (hidden by a later policy/scope
339	change or by a waiver added in the same change) still gates under
340	`baseline-or-current` with `gateReason=code-net-new-policy-hidden`. Verdict is `fail`
341	if any entry gates, else `indeterminate` if any `INDETERMINATE` entry belongs to a
342	gating rule or a current gating rule has unsatisfied/unknown required Coverage or
343	evidence, else `pass`. Rule deficiencies are enumerated independently of findings;
344	zero emitted findings never establish complete analysis. Whole-comparison indeterminacy (unmapped project,
345	unsupported schema/recipe major, context document mismatch) performs no comparison
346	and emits zero entries with a typed remedy. Enum precedence never decides a gate.

350	## 4. Imported evidence: one wrapper, typed payloads (AR-11)
351	
352	There is exactly one import identity: `importId = 'import2:' + H('import', wrapper)`
353	where the wrapper is the foundation `import` descriptor (schemaVersion 2, kinds
354	`runtime|test|history|dependency|prepared`). Each kind admits exactly one canonical
355	payload domain. Native runtime/test/history formats are adapter inputs normalized
356	into the workflow-owned payload before wrapping.
357	
358	| Kind | Admitted payload domain | Owner |
359	|---|---|---|
360	| runtime | `workflow.import-payload.runtime.v1` | workflow |
361	| test | `workflow.import-payload.test.v1` | workflow |
362	| history | `workflow.import-payload.history.v1` | workflow |
363	| dependency | `native.import-payload.dependency-source.v1` | native |
364	| prepared | `native.import-payload.prepared-output.v1` | native |
365	
366	The closed registry names the exact schema document and JSON selector. Its
367	`payloadSchemaDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the entire schema document's bytes;
368	`payloadDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the canonical validated payload. The host validates
369	the selected payload, source correspondence, foundation scope descriptor,
370	BuildIdentityV1, ImportObservationV1 and wrapper using the trusted local schema
371	closure. Merely carrying a recognized payloadDomain is insufficient. Caller-supplied
372	schema bytes must equal the registry document exactly. No network schema resolution
373	is allowed. All auxiliary digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed records;
374	those preimages are retained. The `import2` wrapper alone uses the H-domain recipe.
375	The same payload with different provenance or observation semantics is a different import.
376	
377	Any other pairing is `IMPORT.KIND_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH`; an unregistered payload schema is
378	`IMPORT.PAYLOAD_SCHEMA_UNREGISTERED`; no artifact-supplied schema is ever admitted.
379	`opensip import KIND PATH` is a mutation step with an import receipt; the user-named
380	PATH is a `UserInputPath` opened through the security unit's nofollow custody and
381	never enters identity; every path inside a payload is a strict `LogicalPath`.
382	
383	Source correspondence is mandatory (`IMPORT.MAPPING_REQUIRED`, `CONFIG.INVALID`):
384	the shared closed SourceCorrespondence union in common.schema.json,
385	`exact-snapshot` or `vcs-revision` with VCS/build/mapping fields. Staleness
386	against a Plan is a closed table (`StalenessRule`): snapshot-equal → `current`,
387	consumable; snapshot-differs / commit-differs → `stale`, unmapped-only;
388	commit-equal-dirty → `unverifiable`, unmapped-only; build-identity-differs →
389	`wrong-build`, unmapped-only. An equal clean commit is consumable only with an
390	admitted SourceMappingV1 whose source paths and hashes join the current snapshot
391	inventory; an equal commit without that mapping remains unmapped-only. Corrupt bytes → refused (`IMPORT.ARTIFACT_CORRUPT`).
392	Explicitly selecting a stale import for a Plan is `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`
393	with `IMPORT.STALE_FOR_PLAN` (2). Unmapped-only evidence may be listed and queried
394	but never feeds a predicate.
395	
396	**No-hits is not non-use.** Runtime subjects carry `observed-hit`,
397	`observable-unhit`, `unobservable` or `unmapped`. `observed-hit` supplies positive
398	execution evidence and `observable-unhit` supplies bounded negative evidence,
399	always together with the observation window and population; `unobservable`/`unmapped` never become unhit signals and the schema
400	refuses a hit count on them. One window never establishes universal non-use;
401	runtime coverage is never OpenSIP Coverage. History payloads are advisory priority
402	inputs unless a policy predicate explicitly declares `evidenceUse` for them.
403	
404	**A repair evidence requirement over one of these two relations has its own
405	owning outcome law**, `imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law`
406	(§6). It is separate from native §4.6 because these relations mint no `fact2` and
407	carry no Coverage, and **each kind is projected through its own payload**: a
408	runtime requirement reads `observability`, `observationWindow` and
409	`observedPopulation`; a history requirement reads `revisionRange` and
410	`collectionScope`, which are its bounds fields; `HistoryPayloadV1` also carries
411	subjects and has no runtime observation-window, population or observability
412	fields. Neither kind may report the other's outcomes.
413	
414	**A repair target is a fingerprint, not a path, and the join is published.**
415	`RepairPlanDescriptor.targets` are `finding-key2:` **fingerprints**, while
416	`RuntimeSubject` is keyed by `{path, symbol?}` and `HistorySubject` by `{path}`.
417	The deterministic projection is
418	`imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law/targetSubjectProjection`:
419	each target must be a finding of the evidence Run named by `evidenceRunId` (preview
420	already refuses one that is not); that `finding-key2` identity is the H identity of
421	the retained foundation `finding-fingerprint` descriptor, whose retention is
422	`preimage` and whose bytes are therefore re-hashed at Run closure; and its
423	`subjectKey` supplies the path and qualified name used for matching. The projection
424	does not classify the target by `kind`, whose vocabulary is not closed here. A
425	runtime row matches on path and, if it names a symbol, on qualified name; another
426	symbol's row does not match. A runtime row with no symbol and every history row
427	provide **file** granularity, with `granularityWidenedToFile` disclosed in the
428	projection and successful outcome. A symbol-naming runtime row provides the
429	format's path-and-name granularity, not an exact match of the whole subject key:
430	neither format distinguishes `language`, `kind` or `discriminator`. Distinct
431	findings can therefore project to the same observation. This stated limit applies
432	to every such projection; it cannot establish execution or non-execution of a
433	particular subject variant beyond the captured granularity. More than one
434	matching subject **refuses**: an ambiguous projection is not resolved by choosing
435	one. A target with no matching subject is unsupported — never satisfied, and never
436	read as evidence of non-use.
437	
438	Five limits carry over and are enforced rather than assumed.
439	**Satisfied does not mean positive**: `observed-hit` is positive execution
440	evidence and `observable-unhit` is *bounded negative* evidence, both can satisfy,
441	and the disclosure records which did. **No imported observation establishes a
442	universal negative** — one window is not universal non-use — and imported evidence
443	can never *by itself* establish the native closed world or authorize an unsafe
444	`delete`/`replace`: that gate stays the evidence Run's own `ClosedWorldV2` (§6).
445	It may still be an **additional required condition** alongside an
446	already-established native basis, so it is wrong to say it never affects
447	applicability; an unsatisfied imported requirement makes an otherwise-eligible
448	plan inapplicable. **Whole-versus-partial** is decided by the requirement's
449	`completeness` field: `complete` needs every plan target supported,
450	`partial-acceptable` at least one. That enum already existed, but **this reading of
451	it for an imported requirement over plan targets is selected here** and was not
452	previously published. A target that is unobservable or outside the history
453	collection scope therefore only names the cause *more precisely when the support
454	test fails* — it does not veto a lawful `partial-acceptable` requirement that has a
455	supported target. **Bounds are separate from support**: an insufficient observation
456	window or revision range applies under both completeness values, because it is a
457	property of the observation rather than of the target count. And **required versus
458	optional** stays where `evidenceUse` puts it — an optional absence remains the
459	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE` disclosure and is satisfied *by absence* rather than
460	by evidence. That declaration reaches the requirement boundary as a **typed
461	boolean**; a non-boolean refuses, so there is no `unknown` state to default and no
462	falsy value is read as optional.

466	## 5. Declarative policy DSL, authoring test, candidate → inspect → review
467	
468	**DSL.** `PolicyDocumentV1` is closed data: rules with a `ruleProgramRef`
469	(contribution, stable id, semantics major, program digest), `enabled`, `severity`
470	(`note|warning|error`), `gate`, a `subjectEnumeration` (universe, subject kind,
471	include/exclude globs over `LogicalPath` with only `*`, `?` and whole-segment `**`),
472	an `emitWhen` predicate tree and `evidenceUse` declarations. Predicates are exactly
473	the evaluator's set: atoms `exists|none|count-at-most|all-covered` over a relation,
474	minimum resolution and typed field filters (`eq|neq|in|prefix|glob|gte|lte`), plus
475	`and|or|not`, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 64 nodes per rule, ≤ 512 rules. Evaluation is strong
476	Kleene: under incomplete Coverage `exists` is true on a match else indeterminate,
477	`none` false on a match else indeterminate, `count-at-most` false above N else
478	indeterminate, `all-covered` indeterminate. A true predicate emits a finding; false
479	is a retained no-match; an indeterminate gating rule is a typed deficiency. An atom
480	over imported evidence must be declared in `evidenceUse`; required evidence absent
481	makes the rule indeterminate, optional evidence absent is disclosed as
482	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE` and is not a gating deficiency. There is no string
483	expression, hook, script, include or exec key; any such key is a schema violation
484	(`POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED`). Policy, ScopeDocumentV1 and resolved WaiverSetV1
485	digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed documents, retained as blobs.
486	The compiled RuleProgramV1 separately hashes its policy digest and ordered rule
487	programs to proof.ruleProgramDigest; these are auxiliary hashes, not H identities.
488	
489	**Waivers.** A waiver targets a fingerprint or `(ruleId, subjectPath)` with a reason
490	and `expires` (date or null). Expiry and duplicates are resolved at **Plan
491	construction** against the admitted trust clock: expired waivers leave the effective
492	set and are disclosed (`POLICY.WAIVER_EXPIRED`), two waivers on one target refuse
493	(`POLICY.DUPLICATE_WAIVER`, `CONFIG.INVALID`), and the Plan's `waiverDigest` is that of
494	the *resolved* effective set, keeping evaluation pure. `opensip waive` is the explicit
495	tracked-intent write; nothing writes a waiver implicitly.
496	
497	**Authoring test.** `opensip policy test SUITE` is Query class. A suite supplies the
498	candidate policy, waivers, an `asOfDate`, optional test-only overrides and cases with
499	typed fact fixtures (subjects, facts, declared Coverage, available evidence kinds) or
500	a bounded source fixture. Facts cases are evaluated by the deterministic fixture
501	verifier (the finite declarative fixture evaluator; this is reference evidence, not
502	qualification of the production evaluator or native providers); sources cases run only under an ephemeral non-authoritative Plan with
503	bundled providers and otherwise report `not-executable`. Expectations are
504	`finding{ruleId,minCount,maxCount,subjects}`, `no-finding`, `verdict`, `indeterminate`.
505	The result (`policytest2:`) records candidate and effective digests, resolver
506	acceptance and refusals, applied overrides, waiver resolution and
507	`enforcementUnchanged=true`; the same suite always yields the same result identity.
508	
509	**Candidate → inspect → review (Map side).** `opensip candidates` lists
510	`Candidate` records derived from one sealed Run: findings plus advisory kinds
511	(`clone-candidate`, `low-confidence-unused`, `runtime-unhit`, `history-stale`) with an
512	evidence level. Only a finding on a gating rule is `controlBearing`. `opensip inspect`
513	returns a bounded `InspectionBundle` (≤ 4096 facts, Coverage, imports, limitations).
514	`opensip review join` records a `ReviewDisposition` (`accept|reject|defer`, reviewer
515	principal human/model/policy-rule, note, `suppressUntil` ≤ 365 days) as a mutation
516	with a receipt. The disposition schema admits no verdict, Run, baseline or
517	authorization field: review can never mint a Control verdict or authorize a repair.
518	`reject`/`defer` suppress the candidate from listings until `suppressUntil` or until
519	its fingerprint changes; expired suppressions resurface with `previouslyReviewed`.
520	`opensip review brief` is an advisory, bounded (≤ 1000) ordering labelled with its
521	producer (a model producer names its `closure2`); truncation is explicit.
522

525	## 6. Repair preview, apply, verify (AR-08)
526	
527	Three separately authorized steps; schemas in `repair.schema.json`.
528	
529	**Preview** (`repair-preview`, Query class) requires an **authoritative** evidence Run
530	(`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE` for ephemeral) whose availability is retained
531	and whose sealed assurance is replayable (else the plan is not applicable with
532	`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE`), a recipe closure admitted under current trust
533	(`REPAIR.RECIPE_TRUST_REVOKED`; an absent admission is also refused), targets present in that Run, and a live tree equal to
534	the Run's snapshot (`REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED`). It emits `RepairPlanV1`
535	(`repairplan2:` = `H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)`) bound to `snapshot2`,
536	`run2`, `plan2`, exact per-file edits (`replace|delete|create`, preimage digest from
537	the snapshot inventory, postimage digest and bytes; ≤ 4096 files, ≤ 16 MiB each,
538	≤ 64 MiB total), evidence requirements, the recipe's permitted edit scope (an edit
539	outside it is `REPAIR.EDIT_OUTSIDE_PERMITTED_SCOPE`), `applicable`, unmet
540	preconditions and limitations. Destructive unused-code recipes additionally require
541	native closed-world resolution evidence; an advisory similarity or runtime-cold
542	signal alone never authorizes deletion. Preview never writes.
543	
544	**The closed-world gate reads the evidence Run; the descriptor carries a
545	projection.** The guard covers **every `delete` and every `replace` edit** in the
546	plan — the unsafe-action set is those two actions, without qualification, and this
547	paragraph narrows it in no way. If the plan contains one, the prerequisite is
548	decided against the evidence Run's own native `ClosedWorldV2` (native §4.5) —
549	the record that contract closes at seven members — **before** any descriptor is
550	built: `deadCodeRepairEligible=false` reports
551	`REPAIR.CLOSED_WORLD_NOT_ESTABLISHED` with that record's own `reasons` in the
552	remedy, and an `imported-prepared-declared` evidence origin reports the same code,
553	because a DECLARED prepared expansion is not authority for an unsafe repair.
554	
555	`dynamicDispatch` is **not** a global veto and must not be read as one. Native
556	§4.5 makes dynamic-edge effects **target-relative**: `affected_targets` marks the
557	subjects a dynamic edge could reach, and §4.6 turns that into
558	`resolution-incomplete` for a universal negative **about an affected subject**.
559	So a present dynamic edge disqualifies the claims that depend on the subjects it
560	reaches; it does not by itself disqualify an unrelated target in the same Run.
561	The roles here are distinct and are not merged: preview **admits** each evidence
562	requirement's `relation`/`minResolution` against the registered vocabulary and its
563	relation's own ladder (`admit_atom`, which is vocabulary admission, not an
564	evidence judgement), and then **consumes** that requirement's own `satisfied`
565	value; the semantic sufficiency behind it is owned by native §4.6
566	`sufficiency_v2` and the §4.5 affected-target evidence, per requirement, and is
567	never collapsed into one flag.
568	
569	**Which vocabulary `EvidenceRequirement.deficiency` carries, and when it is
570	required.** Preview admits a requirement over **either evidence plane**, so the
571	field carries the vocabulary of **that requirement's** plane and the plane is
572	decided at admission from the relation's registry membership — the same place the
573	two planes are already separated — never from the value.
574	
575	* **Native plane** — the thirteen native fact relations. The value is native
576	  §4.6's `DeficiencyV2`, named here through the drift-checked mirror
577	  `common.schema.json#/$defs/NativeSufficiencyDeficiency` because this bundle
578	  resolves only its own URNs.
579	* **Imported plane** — `runtime-observation` and `history-change`. Those relations
580	  mint no `fact2` and have no Coverage entry, so `sufficiency_v2` has nothing to
581	  range over and is not asked. Their outcomes are owned by
582	  `imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law` and mirrored
583	  as `common.schema.json#/$defs/ImportedRequirementDeficiency`; every member names
584	  an already-published import condition and is bound to the payload field that
585	  grounds it, and each kind reports only the outcomes **its own** payload can
586	  ground — enforced at **both** the producer and this admission (§4). The
587	  requirement record gains no field: plan `targets` supply the per-target scope
588	  through the published fingerprint projection, `completeness` decides
589	  whole-versus-partial under the reading selected in §4, and `evidenceUse` supplies
590	  required-versus-optional as a typed boolean. The bounded observation demand is
591	  owned by the **admitted recipe closure** named by `recipe.closureId` — `RecipeRef`
592	  carries no such wire field and none is claimed.
593	
594	The two vocabularies are **disjoint**, and a cross-plane value — a native
595	requirement claiming `import-unmapped-only`, or an imported one claiming
596	`resolution-incomplete` — is refused at admission, as is an outcome of the wrong
597	imported **kind**, such as a history range cause on a runtime relation. This schema
598	**deliberately leaves the authoritative registry lookup to admission**: it admits
599	either vocabulary and does not attempt to reproduce the relation registries, which
600	it could not fetch rows from in any case. That is a design choice about where the

601	authority lives, not a limitation of JSON Schema — a schema *can* branch on a
602	property's `const`/`enum` even where the base type is a broader string — and
603	duplicating a registry as schema conditionals would create exactly the drift this
604	contract set avoids elsewhere. The division is stated rather than implied.
605	
606	The value carried is the **satisfaction/deficiency projection** of its producer's
607	result, not that result: `sufficiency_v2` also returns `causes` on both branches
608	and may return `disclosures` on a failing branch. Those are producer result arrays
609	and are fields of no retained record; what is retained is the evidence the
610	evaluation read, so the projection drops nothing that was retained. Presence is **typed**: `deficiency` is **required
611	exactly when `satisfied` is false** and **forbidden when it is true**, `satisfied`
612	must be an actual boolean, and an explicit `null` is refused in both branches
613	because a present key with a null value is not an absent key. Both boundaries — the
614	schema and the preview admission — decide that same law and are held equal on an
615	enumerated shape table. The field previously named
616	`D9Deficiency`, which cannot express four of the nine outcomes its only producer
617	emits — `derivation-policy-unmet`, `external-consumers-unknown`,
618	`input-closure-incomplete` and `resolution-incomplete` — leaving three conforming
619	readings and no document choosing between them: write the D9-mapped value, which
620	is `verdict-indeterminate` for **all four** and so cannot tell
621	`resolution-incomplete` (the outcome §4.6 step 6 mandates for a universal
622	negative under `unresolvedEdgePolicy=forbid` over an affected target, and the one
623	a destructive unused-code recipe turns on) from three unrelated causes; write the
624	sufficiency value and be schema-invalid; or omit the field and drop the
625	disclosure. Retyping this one per-requirement field is the correction.
626	`D9Deficiency` is **unchanged** and still carries every whole-Run and
627	comparison-step termination — three of its members name evaluation, baseline and
628	query outcomes no per-requirement evaluation can produce — and the public D9
629	route for a Run carrying such a requirement is still native §10's. The value is a
630	**disclosure, not an authorization**: `applicable` is false whenever any
631	requirement is unsatisfied, the exact cause is carried into that requirement's
632	unmet precondition so two different causes are two different remedies, the
633	evidence authority remains the sealed Run named by `evidenceRunId`, and any edit
634	to the value mints a different `repairPlanId` that no authorization names.
635	That unmet precondition is emitted once per unsatisfied requirement and carries
636	the existing `REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE` code, which here says that the
637	evidence Run cannot supply what this repair requires and asserts nothing about the
638	Run having been purged or lost — `evidence.purged` and `evidence.missing` keep
639	their own distinct meaning in query results. Preview therefore reaches that one
640	code by two routes, the retained-availability and replayable-assurance failure of
641	the first paragraph above and this per-requirement insufficiency, and the remedy
642	is what tells them apart: the retention entry's remedy names the Run-level
643	restoration that route needs, while the per-requirement entry's remedy names that
644	requirement's `relation`, `minResolution`, evidence plane and exact `deficiency`.
645	`EvidenceRequirement.deficiency` remains the typed cause carrier: no
646	per-deficiency detail code is minted, because the closed public registry is not
647	where a per-requirement outcome vocabulary belongs. An unsatisfied requirement
648	with an empty `unmetPreconditions` is **not** a conforming projection — the schema
649	alone admits that shape, and the emission is decided at admission, the same
650	division of labour already stated for the deficiency vocabulary.
651	
652	`RepairPlanDescriptor.closedWorld` is then the **five-field projection** of the
653	evidence record — `deadCodeRepairEligible`, `exportsClosed`,
654	`entryPointsRecognized`, `nonliteralLoading`, `externalConsumers`, with
655	`dynamicDispatch` and `reasons` dropped — and `repair.schema.json` closes it at
656	exactly those five, so a literal copy of `ClosedWorldV2` is refused there. **The
657	projection grants no evidence authority of its own.** It is a descriptor: no edit
658	to it can make a plan applicable, since the whole descriptor is the preimage of
659	`repairPlanId` (`H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)`) and apply requires a
660	security authorization bound to that exact `repairPlanId`, base snapshot and
661	project. The authority stays the sealed Run named by `evidenceRunId`: the
662	prerequisite above is decided against **that** Run's own full record, including
663	the two members the descriptor does not carry. No claim is made here that a later
664	step re-reads it — `repair verify` seals a **new** Run over the freshly
665	re-snapshotted tree (`appliedSnapshotId` → `verifiedSnapshotId`) and compares
666	remaining and net-new findings; it does not re-open the original evidence Run.
667	
668	**Apply** (`repair-apply`, mutation) is bound to the exact `repairPlanId`, base
669	snapshot and project by a security-unit authorization (`REPAIR.CONSENT_NOT_BOUND`);
670	CI requires policy consent. Current recipe trust and live authorization are checked
671	again immediately before apply. It journals `RepairApplyJournalV1` through
672	`PREPARING → STAGED → APPLYING → APPLIED → COMMITTED`: every postimage is written to a
673	same-directory temp and digest-verified, every preimage is re-verified against the
674	live file (`REPAIR.TARGET_PREIMAGE_MISMATCH` leaves `FAILED_CLEAN`), renames proceed in
675	ascending path order, then the tree is re-snapshotted (`appliedSnapshotId`) and the
676	receipt written. A fault during `APPLYING` restores every renamed target
677	(`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`, rollback `completed`); a renamed target that is neither
678	preimage nor postimage is `RECOVERY_BLOCKED` with the paths listed and no automatic
679	action. Replaying apply with the same idempotency key returns the completed receipt
680	with a new replay delivery receipt and `replayed=true`; the original is preserved.
681	
682	**Recover** (`repair-recover`) is a closed table over journal state: PREPARING/STAGED
683	→ discard temps (`FAILED_CLEAN`); APPLYING → roll back renamed (`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`)
684	or block if a target is unrecognized; APPLIED/INDETERMINATE → verify every exact
685	postimage and the complete applied-path set before re-snapshot and commit;
686	COMMITTED/FAILED_* → none; RECOVERY_BLOCKED → refuse (`HOST.IO_FAILURE`,
687	`REPAIR.RECOVERY_BLOCKED`, exit 4). Every recovery mutation requires an authorization
688	bound to this repairPlanId and journal requestId; inspection alone is read-only.
689	Restore verifies all available retained preimage hashes before its first write.
690	Corrupt bytes yield LEDGER.CORRUPT / REPAIR.PREIMAGE_CORRUPT (4) with no target change.
691	Unavailable bytes return an exact restore intent and REPAIR.RECOVERY_REQUIRES_BROKER,
692	without claiming rollback completed. Recovery never re-applies an edit.
693	
694	**Verify** (`verify`) always admits a **fresh snapshot** after apply; it never reuses
695	the pre-apply Run. If the fresh snapshot differs from `appliedSnapshotId` the step is
696	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED` and no Run is sealed; otherwise
697	it seals a new authoritative Run and reports `VerificationOutcome`
698	(applied/verified snapshot, targets remaining, net-new findings). A separate immutable VerificationLinkV1 binds receiptId, verificationRunId, both
699	snapshots and the verification request/step. The apply receipt is never rewritten
700	and remains retained if verification fails.

704	## 7. Explicitly authorized test execution (AR-08)
705	
706	Repository code execution is disabled by default. `opensip test run` (request class
707	`execution`) is admitted only when: the security unit admits a `RepoExecutionGrantV2`
708	with principal `P-TRUSTED-REPO`, execution class `test-runner`, bound to this
709	project, snapshot digest and the exact `argv` digest, expiry operation-end, never
710	inherited (`TEST.PRINCIPAL_NOT_ADMITTED` otherwise); CI uses a pre-existing policy
711	record (`TEST.INTERACTIVE_CONSENT_IN_CI`); `argv[0]` is a `LogicalPath` member of the
712	sealed snapshot or a member of the declared toolchain `closure2`
713	(`TEST.ARGV_NOT_IN_CLOSURE`); the working directory is the project root or a
714	`LogicalPath` inside it; the environment is constructed from an allowlist only, `PATH`
715	is never copied (`TEST.ENV_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`) and is set to the toolchain closure; and
716	the live tree still equals the `afterStep` snapshot. There is no shell string and no
717	interpolation anywhere in the schema.
718	
719	The step **discloses** and does not confine: `effects.network/subprocess/
720	filesystemWrite` are `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` unless the security unit's platform truth
721	table measures a primitive; a claimed enforcement without a measured primitive is
722	refused (`TEST.CONFINEMENT_CLAIM_REFUSED`). The mandatory sentence before spawn is
723	"Repository test command will run with your user authority. OpenSIP does not prevent
724	network access or other effects on this platform." Output is bounded and truncation
725	is recorded. The outcome is a `TestPayloadV1` wrapped as an `import2` of kind `test`
726	— evidence, never Coverage and never a verdict; a verdict may depend on it only
727	through a declared policy predicate. Imported independently prepared test results
728	are the supported alternative.

733	
734	`workflows/command-inventory.v1.json` is the candidate single inventory,
735	validated by `command-inventory.schema.json`; the checker refuses a command name
736	outside the closed enum and requires every golden to be reachable by the model.
737	
738	| Group | Commands |
739	|---|---|
740	| analysis | `opensip` (default: discovery + durable analyze), `analyze [--ephemeral] [--baseline]`, `fit` (advisory whole-repository report), `audit --baseline [--audit-profile] [--closure-bundle]`, `repair verify` |
741	| query | `recommend` (advisory next-step suggestions from discovery), `query OP`, `baseline show`, `policy show`, `policy test`, `candidates`, `inspect`, `review brief`, `repair preview` |
742	| mutation | `import`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade`, `policy init`, `waive`, `review join`, `repair apply`, `repair recover`, `purge` |
743	| execution | `test run`, `native prepare` (both explicitly authorized) |
744	| lifecycle / serve / meta | `install`, `update`, `core update|repair|rollback`, trust/store commands, `doctor`, `agent serve`, `help`, `version`, `completion` |
745	
746	Only `policy init`, `waive`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade` write tracked intent.
747	Advisory projections never offer SARIF or manufacture a Control verdict. `fit`
748	may run an authoritative analysis by default and then return an advisory report;
749	its underlying sealed Run retains its own verdict.
750	
751	**Renderers.** `human` v1, `json` v2 (the `CommandEnvelope` major 2 is the parity
752	reference), `sarif` v1 (analysis class only; results equal envelope findings
753	one-to-one, verdict/deficiency in run properties), `html` v1 (analysis and query;
754	static single file, no script-fetched data, shows resolution completeness and
755	disclosures), `agent` v1 (the JSON envelope plus `agentHints` that never alter a
756	parity field). Each command names its `parityFields`; every applicable renderer must
757	carry semantically equal values for them. Every advertised SARIF command (`default`,
758	`analyze`, `audit`, `repair-verify`) must declare the common fields `run-id`,
759	`verdict`, `required-coverage`, `deficiency`, `findings`, `termination-class` and
760	`retention-disclosure`; inventory admission refuses an omission. SARIF results
761	and run properties are taken from this same declared host projection, as are
762	human/JSON/HTML/agent values; no renderer reads an undeclared findings field or
763	substitutes null for a present verdict/deficiency. Audit adds its comparison
764	fields while preserving the current analysis result. Repair verification adds
765	applied/verified snapshot, snapshot-match, targets-remaining and net-new-findings
766	fields while preserving the fresh verification Run's findings and verdict.
767	An empty findings array is a real empty result; it is never inferred from a
768	missing projection field. Ephemeral analysis retains its existing no-Run rule:
769	`run-id` is explicitly null in the projection's non-authoritative case,
770	never a fabricated Run. Required-output failure still follows the law below.
771	The host projection must be total over the selected command's `parityFields`
772	before a renderer consumes it: every field has its schema-admitted value,
773	including an explicit null only where that field permits it. A missing field
774	or projection exception is a required-delivery operational fault, not an empty
775	result or a successful partial rendering: `operational-failed`, exit 4,
776	`faultCause=delivery-required`, `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED`. If a Run was already
777	committed, the termination retains its RunId and the after-commit detail below;
778	otherwise no RunId is invented. This classification also covers a pure reference
779	projection helper raising `KeyError`; that exception alone is not a public
780	termination. Actual host exception handling and renderer conformance remain
781	DR-G17/DR-G20 implementation qualification obligations.
782	Requesting a non-applicable format is
783	`REQUEST.UNKNOWN_OPTION` / `OUTPUT.FORMAT_NOT_APPLICABLE` (2). Failure of the selected
784	required renderer **after** a committed Run is `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED` (4) with
785	detail `DELIVERY.RENDERER_FAILED_AFTER_COMMIT`, the `runId` in the termination, and
786	no rewrite of the Run; failure of an optional export sink leaves `success`.

788	**Query.** Twenty closed operations over one sealed view (`run2`, `snapshot2` or the
789	`latest` resolver, whose empty domain is `IDENTITY.UNKNOWN`), bounded page/items/depth/
790	visited nodes; `completeness=required` at a bound is `QUERY.COMPLETENESS_UNMET` (3),

801	absences of an analysis invocation; `DoctorResult.defects[]` remains the
802	environment report it always was.
803	
804	**Release-availability absence rides the invocation that selected it.**
805	`CommandEnvelope.availability` (`CapabilityAvailabilityV1` =
806	`{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[]}`, each step
807	`CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1` = `{stepId, noticeCount, notices[]}`) carries
808	every capability the selected product requires (native §1.4) that this release
809	did not declare available, for **every requested unit of every analysis step** —
810	a single-step command projects one step, and a named multi-step invocation
811	projects one entry per analysis step that made a selection. Each notice carries the complete ownership tuple in **typed
812	fields** — `capabilityId`, `languageMode`, `workspaceRoot` — with the existing

814	condition); the tuple is never concatenated into a `subject`, because
815	`workspaceRoot` is a `UserInputPath` bounded at 4096 while `BoundedText` is 1024
816	and a truncated path would collapse two distinct units into one indistinguishable

818	`{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[≤64]}`, each step
819	`{stepId, noticeCount, notices[≤1024]}` — because 1024 is the
820	`analysis-spec.requestedCapabilities` bound and *not* an invocation-wide one: two
821	admitted selections of 1023 requests each compose 2046 notices, and no notice is
822	discarded to fit. A step that made no selection contributes no entry, a step that
823	found nothing absent contributes an empty entry, and the same tuple may recur in

826	Envelope membership alone would **not** deliver it: `render` selects a command's
827	declared `parityFields`, so `capability-availability` is a declared parity field

832	whose invocation selected nothing supplies the explicit empty collection
833	(`{stepCount: 0, totalNoticeCount: 0, steps: []}`) rather than omitting the
834	field, and an omission is a required-delivery operational fault under the law
835	above, never a successful partial rendering.
836

839	Candidate records represent actual candidates. `AnalysisResult` is a closed union
840	and is not widened to carry it.

56	## S3. Discovery and custody (AR-03)
57	
58	Discovery is deterministic over lstat/ACL results obtained through O_NOFOLLOW
59	handles: no environment variable, no `PATH`, no `HOME` (the account home comes
60	from the account database). Output is the closed `DiscoveryProvenanceV1`.
61	
62	The disposable discovery instrument accepts only its named host-observation keys:
63	required `invokingUid`, `accountHome`, `cwd`, `fs`; optional `ci`,
64	`trustProjectOwner`, `authorizedGroupIds`, `explicitProject`, `explicitResolved`,
65	`explicitJoins`, `configWorkspaceRoots`. Unknown/missing keys or wrong outer
66	scalar/container types are `DISCOVERY_OBSERVATION_SHAPE` instrument errors,
67	not public D9 input refusals. Boolean observations are exact booleans and uid/gid
68	observations are nonnegative integers, never coerced strings or booleans. The
69	lstat/ACL map remains a synthetic trusted observation, not proof of native custody.
70	Public invocation/configuration admission still precedes this host-only seam.
71	
72	**Custody of a directory** passes only if: it is a real directory (no symlink);
73	owner is the invoking uid or root; mode has no other-write bit; mode has no
74	group-write bit unless the directory's gid is in the explicitly authorized set;
75	no ACL write grant (POSIX ACL on Linux, `acl_get_fd_np` on macOS) to any
76	principal other than the invoker, root, or an authorized group; and the ACL was
77	readable. Mode bits alone never establish exclusion. **Custody of a config
78	file** adds: regular file, link count 1, at most 4 MiB. Group authorization
79	exists only through an explicit `--trust-group <gid>` invocation argument and
80	is recorded in provenance; configuration cannot grant it. `--trust-project-owner`
81	waives only the owner check and only with an explicit `--project` path.
82	
83	**Walk rule.** With `--project`, the resolved path is examined exactly once
84	(symlink resolution recorded). Otherwise, from the launch directory upward, at
85	most 256 levels: a custody failure at the launch directory refuses
86	(`PROJECT.ROOT_CUSTODY_REFUSED`); a custody failure at an ancestor is a
87	boundary and that ancestor is never examined for a config. At each passing
88	directory the config, if present, is custody-checked (failure refuses
89	`CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED`; it is never skipped) and selects that directory
90	(`mode: config`). Boundaries after a directory without config, in precedence:
91	VCS marker (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.jj`), account home, filesystem root, mount
92	change. A VCS boundary selects **that repository root** (`mode: vcs-default`),
93	never the launch directory, so default scope does not change with launch
94	directory. Home, root, mount and custody boundaries without any candidate
95	select the launch directory (`mode: cwd-default`).
96	
97	**Nested config is a deliberate project boundary (decided; ADV-3).** A config
98	file found below a VCS root is an author-declared project root and wins for
99	launches inside it; the walk never continues above a config. The enclosing
100	VCS-root project treats that directory exactly like a nested repository: it is
101	recorded in `nestedProjects`, automatic discovery never enters it (excluded
102	unit reason `INSIDE_NESTED_PROJECT`), and an explicit join crossing into it
103	refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_PROJECT`). Scope
104	therefore depends only on which project a launch is inside, never on which
105	directory of one project. The alternative (VCS root always wins) was rejected
106	because it would silently ignore a config the repository author placed. Cases
107	`nested-config-inside-a-vcs-root-*` and
108	`explicit-join-crossing-into-a-nested-project-refuses`.
109	
110	**VCS data.** A `.git` indirection file (`gitdir:`) is data: its target is
111	recorded and never followed by discovery; VCS digests for the snapshot are the
112	identity unit's concern and read only inside custody.
113	
114	**Authority roots versus workspace units.** Two different things are
115	distinguished. A *project authority/custody root* is the selected root: one
116	custody domain, one ProjectId, one lease namespace. Repositories nested under
117	it are other custody roots: they are recorded as `nestedRepositories`, never
118	entered, and reachable only by their own `--project`; a join that crosses into
119	one refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_REPOSITORY`).
120	A *language workspace unit* is a directory inside the admitted root that
121	carries a manifest marker: `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` or
122	`jsconfig.json` (markers may co-locate; a unit lists all its markers). Units are
123	discovered **automatically** for the zero-config full product, with precedence:
124	
125	| Source | Provenance `unitSource` | Custody failure |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| repeatable CLI `--workspace-root PATH` overrides | `explicit-joins` | refuses (explicit intent) |
128	| admitted Config2 `discovery.workspaceRoots` (foundation product-configuration schema v2) | `config-workspace-roots` | refuses |
129	| marker scan of the admitted root | `automatic` | unit excluded, recorded in `excludedUnits` with the reason |
130	
131	An explicit source suppresses automatic discovery. Every directory from the
132	root to a unit must pass directory custody and stay inside the root (no
133	absolute, `.`, `..`, backslash or NUL segments); every marker file must pass
134	file custody. A manifest is **data**: discovery records its presence and later
135	readers parse it as data only, never running scripts, hooks, plugins or
136	workspace globs and never writing source.
137	
138	**One shared discovery rule (MUST-3).** The zero-config rule is stated once, in
139	`docs/coop/design-corrections/discovery-defaults.py`, and consumed by this
140	instrument and by the native unit instrument (native §1.4); neither restates
141	it. Before any custody walk, automatic discovery prunes, by **exact path
142	segment** (never substring): dependency trees (a segment `node_modules`), VCS
143	trees (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.jj`) and Cargo build output (a segment
144	`target` whose parent directory holds `Cargo.toml`, an actual Cargo root; a
145	source directory merely called `target`, such as `packages/target` or
146	`src/target`, is ordinary source). A pruned tree yields no unit, no marker,
147	no custody walk and no program member; its anchor is recorded **once** in
148	`prunedTrees` with the number of markers it hid, so 4200 installed package
149	manifests are one record, never 4200 units. A `Cargo.toml` inside a pruned
150	tree does not create a Cargo root. First-party unit directories are capped at
151	4096; exceeding the cap refuses typed `PROJECT.WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT` (D9
