517	### 1.4 Mixed repositories and workspace units (R1)
518	
519	The v1 rule ("deepest root, then `Cargo.toml` > `tsconfig.json`") was wrong: in a
520	repository whose root holds both `Cargo.toml` and `package.json`/`tsconfig.json`
521	every TypeScript file fell into the Rust unit and silently left the TypeScript
522	program. Units are now **per language family and program membership**, and may
523	share a root.
524	
525	**Reference discovery model** (`discover_units`, `assign_membership` in the model;
526	records `WorkspaceUnitV2`, `FileMembershipRowV1`, `UnitMembershipV1`). The root
527	discovery boundary and trust decision remain the security/foundation owners'
528	(DR-103); this contract defines what happens inside that boundary.
529	
530	`WorkspaceUnitV2` (closed): `{unitOrdinal, rootPath, languageFamily: rust|tsjs|none,
531	languageMode, unitKind: cargo-workspace|cargo-package|ts-program|js-program|syntax-only,
532	markerPath, markerSha256, recognizerId, recognizerVersion, provenance:
533	EXPLICIT|DISCOVERED|DEFAULTED, memberPackageRoots[]}`.
534	
535	- **U-1 (one unit per directory and language family)** A directory holding
536	  `Cargo.toml` yields a `rust` unit; a directory holding `tsconfig.json`,
537	  `jsconfig.json` or `package.json` yields exactly one `tsjs` unit whose mode is
538	  chosen by precedence `tsconfig.json` (→ `ts-tsconfig`/`js-allowjs`) >
539	  `jsconfig.json` (→ `js-allowjs`) > `package.json` (→ `js-synthesized`). The
540	  precedence selects the mode **within** `tsjs`; it never removes the co-located
541	  `rust` unit. A root with both markers has two units with the same `rootPath`
542	  (`units-colocated-cargo-and-package-json-root-keeps-both-languages`).
543	- **U-2 (Cargo workspace folding)** A `Cargo.toml` package inside a Cargo
544	  workspace root's tree is folded into the workspace unit as a member package
545	  (Cargo resolves the workspace as one program); it is listed in
546	  `memberPackageRoots`, not as a separate unit. A standalone package outside any
547	  workspace is its own `cargo-package` unit. **Explicit roots are unit
548	  selection, never loss of Cargo workspace semantics (post-reset v2 A-3/P22):**
549	  naming a Cargo workspace root explicitly yields exactly the automatic result
550	  for that unit (members folded, member `target` output pruned, a member's
551	  `src/target` still source); naming a member package alone selects that package
552	  as its own `cargo-package` unit, and files of the unselected root or siblings
553	  are honest `no-program-unit-for-language` rows, neither claimed nor
554	  over-ignored (`units-explicit-cargo-workspace-root-keeps-member-folding-and-member-target-pruning`).
555	- **U-3 (deterministic membership within a language)** A file's family is fixed
556	  by extension (`.rs` → `rust`; `.ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` → `tsjs`).
557	  It belongs to the **deepest unit of its own family** whose root prefixes its
558	  path. Units of another family never claim it. Nested monorepo packages
559	  (`packages/web/tsconfig.json` under a root `tsconfig.json`) are therefore
560	  distinct `tsjs` units and the deeper one wins for its subtree
561	  (`units-nested-monorepo-deepest-within-language-and-workspace-folding`).

563	  file appears in exactly one `FileMembershipRowV1`: `program-member`;

699	`analysis-spec.requestedCapabilities[].capabilityId` was `$ref: Text` and enters
700	`PlanId` through `analysisSpecDigest`, and no document named the vocabulary it is

701	drawn from. Three spellings were consequently in live use in one release: the

712	  closed at eleven members, with the law published beside it at
713	  `#/capabilityIdLaw`. The same vocabulary serves
714	  `product-configuration.analysis.capabilities`, whose item pattern
715	  `^[a-z][a-z0-9._:-]*$` already contained no `@` — so the `relation@rung`
716	  spelling was never admissible at the configuration layer and is now refused by
717	  shape at the analysis-spec layer too, before membership is consulted.
718	- **A capability id is not a `relation@rung`.** They are different concepts and
719	  are not equated. A capability is a *requestable unit of work* and may cover
720	  several relations (`inventory` covers `file@enumerated`,
721	  `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported`; `syntax` covers the
722	  three syntactic rungs) or none at all (`clones-near` and `clones-cross-tsjs`

725	  grammar-capability registry and the relation ladders speak. The bridge in both
726	  directions is the matrix's own `capabilities[].relations`, so an implementer
727	  never has to guess one from the other.

729	  The `(capability, mode)` cell must exist — the table is the complete product of
730	  the eleven capabilities and the six modes, so it always does for registered
731	  members — and its state must not be `NOT-SELECTED`, which means "outside D-371;
732	  no promise" and is an *unsatisfiable* request rather than a disclosable one.

734	  requestable and is answered with `unknown` plus its own named deficiency and
735	  cause, never refused. Today's three `NOT-SELECTED` cells are
736	  `clones-cross-tsjs` under `rust-cargo`, `rust-cargo-prepared` and `syntax-only`.

738	  input — which rows a release ships is not a contract constant — but its schema

743	  `capabilityId` refuses rather than merging, because two rows declaring

747	  is the *release declaration's*; the **request** had no analogue, and it needed

769	  `x-opensip-uniqueness`) and enforced in `admit_requested_capabilities`, the one

795	said "the registry may declare a **subset** of the matrix — a release need not

804	- **Required default (fixed by the matrix, not by a release).** For each
805	  discovered unit the `default` profile **must** request every capability whose

807	  definition of the selected product, since `NOT-SELECTED` means "outside D-371;

811	  answers with the disclosed unavailable pair. Omitting it would leave a consumer
812	  with no record that the capability exists and was not served.
813	- **Absence is disclosed, not dropped — and delivered.** A capability the product
814	  requires and this release does not declare available is still requested, and the
815	  selection boundary records the absence in `default_capability_selection`'s
816	  `undeclaredCapabilities`. That record is an **availability account, not a
817	  `CoverageResultV3`** and not a final `(deficiency, nativeCause)` pair — and, on
818	  its own, it is a helper return, not something a consumer receives. An earlier
819	  revision stopped there and called it "machine-readable"; an in-memory result is
820	  not a delivered disclosure.

822	  analysis step's selection produces the `{noticeCount, notices[]}` leaf
823	  (`release_absence_notices`); adding its `stepId` forms a
824	  `CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1`, and the invocation's steps compose
825	  `CapabilityAvailabilityV1` = `{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[]}`
826	  (`invocation_availability`), carried on **`CommandEnvelope.availability`**.
827	  Each notice carries the **complete ownership tuple in typed fields** —
828	  `capabilityId`, `languageMode` and the unit's own `workspaceRoot` — with the
829	  code `native.capability-unavailable` and the registered remedy. Two things this
830	  fixes: an earlier revision concatenated `<capabilityId> @ <languageMode>` into
831	  a `subject` and **discarded `workspaceRoot`**, so two units requesting the same
832	  capability collapsed into one indistinguishable notice; and it had no carrier
833	  for *multiple* absences in the original invocation at all, since
834	  `StepTermination.domainDetail` is singular and a `doctor` report is a
835	  **different invocation**. The tuple is never concatenated: `workspaceRoot` is a
836	  `UserInputPath` bounded at 4096 while `BoundedText` is 1024, so concatenation
837	  could silently truncate a path.
838	- **Composed per step, because 1024 is the analysis-spec bound.** Each analysis
839	  step's own selection becomes a `CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1`
840	  (`{stepId, noticeCount, notices[≤1024]}`), and the invocation carries
841	  `{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[≤64]}`. A *step's* collection cannot
842	  truncate — 1024 is exactly the `analysis-spec.requestedCapabilities` bound and
843	  one selection yields at most one absence per requested row — but the invocation
844	  is **not** bounded by that number: a named multi-step invocation carries up to
845	  64 steps, and two admitted selections of 1023 requests each compose 2046
846	  notices, which one flat 1024 array refused. Composing per step preserves every
847	  valid admitted invocation and **discards no notice to fit**; `steps` is bounded
848	  by the invocation's own step bound (`StepId` 0–63).
849	- **Association, order and count.** Each entry names the `stepId` whose selection
850	  produced it. A step that made **no** selection contributes no entry; a step
851	  that selected and found nothing absent contributes an entry with an **empty**
852	  array, which is the positive statement that it checked; a retried step
853	  contributes one entry, for the attempt whose selection the invocation retained.
854	  The same ownership tuple may recur in **different** steps, so uniqueness is
855	  within a step and never across the invocation. `noticeCount` equals each step's

859	  widened.
860	- **The notice's code is its condition.** `code` is `const
861	  native.capability-unavailable`, not the whole `DomainDetailCode` enum: this

863	  `CONFIG.INVALID` on a release-absence notice.
864	- **Declared parity, not merely envelope membership.** Being present on the
865	  envelope does not make a field part of renderer parity — `render` selects only
866	  a command's declared `parityFields`, so the collection reached JSON and agent
867	  and was omitted by human, SARIF and HTML. `capability-availability` is now a
868	  declared parity field of every `requestClass: analysis` command (`default`,
869	  `analyze`, `fit`, `audit`, `repair-verify`), so every applicable renderer
870	  carries it.
871	- **Authority limits.** The disclosure is **advisory**: it terminates nothing,
872	  mints no Coverage, creates no Control verdict and no repair authority, and
873	  fabricates no clone `Candidate` — the published Candidate records represent
874	  actual candidates, so an absent provider can never be one. Nothing here
875	  truncates: a step's `notices` is bounded by the analysis-spec request bound it
876	  can never exceed, and `steps` by the invocation's own step bound, so
877	  `noticeCount` and `totalNoticeCount` are exact rather than a residue of a
878	  dropped tail.
879	- **Which capabilities use which route.** A **fact-producing** capability keeps
880	  its `relation@rung` Coverage under the existing precedence, and this detail
881	  does not replace it. A **candidate-only** capability has no Coverage entry at
882	  all, so this detail is its *only* public route. No new vocabulary, no new
883	  public code, **no preview or default exception**.
884	- **What an absence projects to, and what wins when two apply.** Neither case may
885	  be assumed. *Precedence*: a capability can be undeclared **and** unservable by
886	  the admitted universe at once — `references` under `syntax-only` is both. The
887	  syntax capability prerequisite *derives* `language-tier-unsupported` /
888	  `capability-missing` for such a scope and refuses anything else, and §10's
889	  precedence ranks `language-tier-unsupported` ahead of `provider-unavailable`,
890	  so the more specific one wins and the release-absence account never overrides
891	  it. Where no more specific deficiency applies, `provider-unavailable` with
892	  `capability-missing` is the applicable pair on the existing
893	  `COVERAGE.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` route. *Candidate-only capabilities*:
894	  `clones-near` and `clones-cross-tsjs` have **empty** matrix `relations` — they
895	  are candidate-only by §6.1 authority, mint no fact and no `relation@rung`, and
896	  therefore have **no Coverage entry** that could carry a pair; requiring one
897	  would mean fabricating a relation. Their account is the selection record itself
898	  (`projection: selection-account-only`), while fact-producing capabilities carry
899	  `projection: coverage-entry` and name the exact `relation@rung` coordinates
900	  they project onto. An availability account may be shared by all capabilities;
901	  it is automatically a Coverage result for none of them.
902	- **Availability is not qualification.** Declaring a capability cannot promote a
903	  cell: `platformQualified` stays false, no cell is `QUALIFIED`, and
904	  `SUPPORTED-DESIGN` remains "contracted behavior, corpus named, qualification
905	  pending" whatever a release declares. A staged or development build shipping
906	  fewer providers is an availability fact disclosed per request — not a narrowed
907	  product and not a completed release qualification.
908	- **Explicit configuration overrides the request, not the obligation.**
909	  `product-configuration.analysis.capabilities` uses this same vocabulary; an
910	  override is a recorded choice with its own provenance (the default's is
911	  `DEFAULTED`). A user narrowing their own analysis is visible; a host silently
912	  narrowing the product would not be.
913	- **The host input boundary, honestly.** *Which* rows a release ships is an
914	  authenticated input this contract cannot measure, and nothing here qualifies a
915	  build, an installer or a provider. What is contract is the obligation the
916	  default must meet, the membership the declaration is held to, and the
917	  disclosure an absence owes.
918	- **Closed at admission, not only in the helper.** The default helper is one
919	  producer of an `analysis-spec`, not the authority. The same vocabulary is
920	  closed again at Plan/Run closure over the **retained** `analysis-spec`

922	  configured or hand-built spec is judged by exactly the rule a defaulted one is,

924	  foundation keeps its own fault for an unregistered *mode*; native owns which
925	  capabilities exist and which cells this product promises anything for.
926	
927	No capability is added, removed or renamed, no cell state changes, and all six
928	advertised modes, the three native contexts and the full default-selected

930	for a field that had none.

947	## 2. Semantic universe successors
948	
949	Every array in the current native schema bundle declares `x-opensip-order`
950	under identity §3. `sequence` preserves order and repeated items unless a separate
951	uniqueness constraint applies. It is intentional for compiler flags, signature
952	tokens, substitution precedence and ordered observations. Stricter orders are
953	machine-checked at schema admission: declaration components by `component`,
954	dependency packages by `(name, version, sourceId)`, owner records by `ownerKey`,
955	file-manifest rows by `path`, and the explicitly sorted path/name/enum collections
956	by raw UTF-8 bytes. These keys must be unique; a second row with the same key and
957	different payload also refuses. The canonical encoder never sorts a collection.
958	Input-adapter observation sequences retain their own declared order; a producer
959	must construct any stricter output collection before admitting it.

985	**Binding a `rust-v2` universe (`bind_rust_universe`).** A universe is bound to its

987	`bind_typescript_universe` (§2.4), and for the same reason: an identity commits to
988	the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them. The binding is pure — it

993	no context-free or input-free admit path, because an optional join is not a rule,

1019	### 2.2 `typescript-v2` (replaces `typescript-v1.resolvedInputs`)
1020	
1021	Retained **in the universe**: `tsconfigGraphHash`, `programRootFiles`,
1022	`executionCapableResolution` (constant `false`: no TypeScript-side repository
1023	execution is selected).
1024	
1025	**Relocated to the context** (§2.4), and therefore *not* fields of the closed
1026	`TypeScriptUniverseV2ResolvedInputs`, which is `additionalProperties: false`:
1027	`compilerOptions` — now `TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2.honoredOptions` and
1028	`strippedOptions`; `packageLockIdentity` — now
1029	`TypeScriptNativeContextV2.lockfileIdentity`, with `lockfileKind` retained in the
1030	universe as its kind projection; and `resolvedNodeModulesLayout` — now the
1031	retained `ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1` record that
1032	`TypeScriptNativeContextV2.nodeModulesLayoutDigest` names. An implementer building
1033	a universe record from the older "Retained:" list produced a record that fails
1034	admission; these three moved, they were not dropped.
1035	
1036	`tsconfigGraphHash` is the **raw SHA-256 of `C(TypeScriptConfigGraphV1)`** — a
1037	retained canonical record, not an H identity and not an opaque id. That record is
1038	`{schemaVersion: 1, entryConfigPath, nodes}`, where `nodes` is the strictly ascending
1039	unique-by-`path` array of every config file actually read, each
1040	`{path, contentSha256, kind, extendsResolved}`: `contentSha256` is that file's
1041	inventoried snapshot digest and `extendsResolved` is the ordered array of
1042	project-relative paths its `extends` entries resolved to. Later entries take
1043	precedence; repetitions are retained, and an empty array means no base config.
1044	`entryConfigPath` selects the root config, or is null for synthesized configuration.
1045	The record is a **required** binding input, and the binding
1046	checks that `nodes[].path` is exactly the context's
1047	`configProjection.configGraphPaths` set, that every node's digest is the snapshot's,
1048	and that every edge names another node. Every node must be reachable from the
1049	selected entry and the graph must be acyclic, so the universe key and the context
1050	cannot describe two different config graphs.
1051	
1052	`configOrigin` is **derived from that retained record, never asserted**:
1053	`synthesized` exactly when the entry is null and `nodes` is empty; otherwise it
1054	comes from the selected entry's kind (`jsconfig` for a jsconfig entry, otherwise
1055	`tsconfig`). A jsconfig entry extending a shared base remains a jsconfig program.
1056	The universe's `configOrigin` must equal the derived value. This is the input
1057	§2.4's agreement check needs; without the record the `tsconfig`/`jsconfig`
1058	distinction was not derivable and two spellings minted two universe identities for
1059	one admitted context.
1060	
1061	**Node `kind` is derived from the node's path by a published closed table, for
1062	every node.** The rule is
1063	`native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-config-node-kind-law`, named by an
1064	`x-opensip-vocabulary` annotation on the field itself: take the **basename** —
1065	the final `/`-separated segment — and compare it **exactly and case-sensitively**;
1066	`tsconfig.json` → `tsconfig`, `jsconfig.json` → `jsconfig`, **every other
1067	basename → `other`**. No prefix, glob or stem matching, no case folding, nothing
1068	read from the file's content, its depth or its position in the graph. It applies
1069	to the **entry and to every non-entry node** alike:
1070	`packages/web/tsconfig.json` reached as a base is `tsconfig`, and
1071	`tsconfig.build.json` reached as a base is `other` — the widespread
1072	`tsconfig*.json` naming convention is deliberately **not** the rule, because the
1073	exact table is total and decidable from the retained path alone while a prefix
1074	rule would additionally have to decide `jsconfig.build.json`, an extensionless
1075	`tsconfig` and `tsconfig.jsonc`. `other` is an ordinary value, not a defect: an explicitly selected custom-named configuration is an `other` entry that
1076	still derives `configOrigin=tsconfig`.
1077	
1078	This had to be written down rather than left to "the schema and native
1079	admission", which stated it nowhere. `kind` is **inside the hashed record** —
1080	`tsconfigGraphHash` is the raw SHA-256 of `C(TypeScriptConfigGraphV1)`, the
1081	universe requires it, and the universe identity reaches `fact2`, `scope2`,
1082	`coverage2`, `view2`, `evidence2`, `seal2` and the RunId — while `configOrigin`
1083	reads only the entry's kind and therefore pins nothing, and a non-entry node's
1084	kind derives no value at all. Two conforming hosts reading one repository that
1085	contains `tsconfig.build.json` would have minted two RunIds and defeated
1086	independent replay across machines, which is the same defect the analysis-spec
1087	`capabilityId` vocabulary was closed for and is closed the same way. A node whose
1088	declared kind is not the derived one refuses
1089	(`native.config-graph-kind-contradicts-path`), so neither the entry nor a base can
1090	be relabelled. A candidate digest may already have been computed and compared when
1091	that fault is raised — the universe is simply never **admitted**, and no identity
1092	is accepted, while any fault stands.
1093

1096	`checkJs`, `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `jsDiagnosticsEnabled`,
1097	`resolutionCompletenessImplied=false`, `jsRootFiles`, `lockfileKind`,

1100	`nativeContextId` — the identity of the **`TypeScriptNativeContextV2`** record of §2.4,

1102	(that record is the Rust context, §2.3), and a `typescript-v2` universe that names a

1124	specifier is an `unresolved-module-specifier` edge with scope `external` — never an

1129	`package.json`; version 1 pinned): `allowJs=true`, `checkJs=false`,

1136	### 2.3 `NativeContextV2` (Rust)
1137	
1138	**There is exactly one native-context record and one `H` domain per language.**
1139	`NativeContextV2` is the **Rust** context; `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (§2.4) is the
1140	TypeScript one. Neither is a general "native context": a universe binds the record of its
1141	own language and refuses the other.
1142	
1143	Descriptor (domain `native.context.rust.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, targetTriple,
1144	hostTriple, toolchain: ToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: ToolClosureV1, baseCfg,
1145	resolverVersion, dependencySourceSetId, unifiedFeaturesId, preparedOutputSetId|null,
1146	configProjection: CargoConfigProjectionV2}`.
1147	
1148	`rustcDevLlvmDigest` is at **`NativeContextV2.toolchain.rustcDevLlvmDigest`**, inside
1149	`ToolchainIdentityV1` — not a top-level field of the context (a citation that says only "in
1150	native-context schema 2" is reachable but under-specified). Its value is the 64-hex suffix
1151	of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=rust-dev-llvm` closure, so `"closure2:" +`
1152	the field must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it;
1153	`admit_native_context('rust', …)` performs exactly that join against the retained closure
1154	descriptor and tree.
1155	
1156	`ToolClosureV1` = `{rustc, cargo, linker|null, ar|null, procMacroServer, closureId}`
1157	— the raw digests of every executable the adapter may select, all members of the
1158	signed `closure2` named by `closureId`. **Every tool that runs is in this
1159	closure**: `rustc`, `cargo`, the linker rustc spawns when a build script or
1160	proc-macro crate is linked, `ar`, and the proc-macro server. No `PATH` lookup, no
1161	system `cc`, no `RUSTC`/`CARGO`/`RUSTUP_*`/`CARGO_HOME` from the environment. If a
1162	platform family has no bundled linker in the closure, in-host preparation is
1163	`UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` there (`native.execution-not-authorized`, cause
1164	`linker-unavailable`); it never falls back to a system linker.
1165	
1166	The host resolved-inputs adapter computes the context before PlanId; the worker
1167	recomputes it after sealed inputs are received and refuses with
1168	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze if any byte differs (§9.5).

1170	### 2.4 `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (TypeScript/JavaScript)

1172	Descriptor (domain `native.context.typescript.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, languageMode,
1173	toolchain: TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: TypeScriptToolClosureV1,
1174	configProjection: TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2, moduleResolutionMode, packageModuleType,

1177	`TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1` = `{compilerName:"typescript", compilerVersion,

1179	libSelection[]}`. `TypeScriptToolClosureV1` = `{compiler, runtime, closureId}`.

1181	**Exact field locations and producing recipe.** Every value is computed by the host
1182	resolved-inputs adapter before PlanId from **admitted, retained** bytes; none is read from a
1183	worker claim, a `tsc --version` string or the environment.
1184	
1185	| Field | Produced from |
1186	|---|---|
1187	| `toolchain.compilerVersion` | the `semanticVersion` of the **admitted signed compiler closure manifest** named by `toolClosure.closureId`; admission refuses when the two differ, so a version string and the bytes it labels cannot drift apart |
1188	| `toolchain.compilerPackageDigest` | a member digest of that retained `kind=toolchain` closure tree |
1189	| `toolchain.typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` | identity §3's existing recipe: the **64-hex suffix** of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=stdlib` closure. `"closure2:" +` the value must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it |
1190	| `toolchain.standardLibraryComponentDigests` | the **complete** declaration-file inventory of that retained stdlib tree — one row per `.d.ts` member, selected or not, `component` = the member basename, sorted by `component`. A tree in which two paths share a basename refuses `native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<name>` rather than resolving the join arbitrarily |
1191	| `toolchain.libSelection` | the effective `lib` **names** the resolved `compilerOptions` select after `target` defaulting, sorted; each must map to a retained component under the published name-to-component join below. These are `lib` names (`es2022`), never declaration-file names |
1192	| `toolClosure.compiler`, `toolClosure.runtime` | raw digests of the bundled compiler and of the bundled JavaScript runtime that executes it, both members of the signed closure named by `closureId`. No `PATH` lookup, no system `node`, no `NODE_OPTIONS`/`NODE_PATH`/`TS_NODE_*` from the environment |
1193	| `configProjection.honoredOptions` | the closed subset of the **effective** resolved `compilerOptions` (or of `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` under `js-synthesized`) that changes program membership, module resolution or checking |
1194	| `configProjection.strippedOptions` | every option removed, with a typed reason (`selects-an-executable`, `emits-output`, `reads-the-environment`, `acquires-types-from-the-network`, `not-a-resolution-or-membership-option`). 1195	| `configProjection.configGraphPaths` | every `tsconfig`/`jsconfig` file of the resolved `extends` graph, in the snapshot, sorted by logical path; empty under `configOrigin=synthesized` |
1196	| `nodeModulesLayoutDigest` | raw SHA-256 of `C(ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1)` — the retained resolution read-set layout — or `null` exactly when `nodeModulesInReadSet=false` |

1198	
1199	**Retained trees.** The stdlib closure and the compiler closure are retained **whole** —
1200	complete foundation `closure` descriptor and complete file tree — and joined to the selected
1201	compiler. `admit_native_context` recomputes each closure identity from its retained record
1202	and refuses `native.native-context-closure-unretained`,
1203	`native.native-context-closure-identity-mismatch` or
1204	`native.native-context-closure-kind-mismatch` before any digest comparison. The stdlib merkle
1205	root is therefore never a bare number a caller can assert.
1206	
1207	**`libSelection` → `standardLibraryComponentDigests`: the published join.** The
1208	two arrays hold different vocabularies on purpose and neither is rewritten into
1209	the other. `libSelection` holds effective **`lib` names** — the values
1210	`configProjection.honoredOptions.lib` carries (`es2022`, `dom`), which is why the
1211	two are compared directly. `standardLibraryComponentDigests[].component` holds
1212	**declaration-file basenames** of the retained stdlib closure tree
1213	(`lib.es2022.d.ts`). Because the join between them is enforced at context
1214	admission with its own typed refusal, it is published here rather than left to
1215	ecosystem convention; two hosts inventing different mappings would admit and
1216	refuse the *same* retained context bytes differently, which is a public admission
1217	divergence, not implementation freedom.
1218	
1219	| Rule | Statement |
1220	|---|---|
1221	| Fold | `fold(n)` is Unicode **Default Case Conversion `toLowercase(X)`**: the **full**, **non-tailored**, **context-sensitive** default lowercase mapping (Unicode Standard §3.13 / UAX #21). It is the **same single fold** the honored-`lib` agreement below uses, and this section defines no other: no NFC/NFKC step, no trimming, no alias table, no prefix or suffix matching. Reference implementation `native_evidence_model.v2.lib_name_fold` |
1222	| Mapping | `component(n) = "lib." + fold(n) + ".d.ts"`. Total, deterministic and **one-directional**: a selected name maps to exactly one component basename, and a component is never mapped back into a selected name |
1223	| Membership | for every `n` in `libSelection`, `component(n)` must be an element of the declared `component` set. A name whose component is absent refuses `native.native-context-lib-not-retained:<n>` — §10 route `request-rejected` (2) / `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, before PlanId |
1224	| Equality | `{fold(n) : n ∈ libSelection}` must equal `{fold(m) : m ∈ honoredOptions.lib}`. `honoredOptions.lib` is required and non-empty in the closed resolved context, so this agreement always applies and is **not** weakened by the mapping. Two `libSelection` entries with the same fold refuse `native.native-context-field-mismatch:duplicate-lib-selection`; a set disagreement refuses `native.native-context-field-mismatch:libSelection` |
1225	| Order | `libSelection` is sorted by the raw UTF-8 bytes of the **retained, unfolded** names; `standardLibraryComponentDigests` by the raw UTF-8 bytes of `component`. Each record keeps its own specified order for hashing — folding is a comparison, never a rewrite of a retained value, and neither array is re-spelled into the other's vocabulary |
1226	
1227	**What `fold` is, and what it is not.** The three plausible operations are genuinely different
1228	and only one of them is the one this admission performs, so it is named rather than approximated.
1229	
1230	| Discriminator | `fold` (**full default lowercase**) | simple lowercase | case folding |
1231	|---|---|---|---|
1232	| `U+0130` LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE | `U+0069 U+0307` — **two** code points, through `SpecialCasing.txt` | `U+0069`, one code point | `U+0069 U+0307` |
1233	| `U+039F U+03A3` (sigma in **final** position) | `U+03BF U+03C2` — the `Final_Sigma` condition | `U+03BF U+03C3` | `U+03BF U+03C3` |
1234	| `U+03A3 U+039F` (sigma **not** final) | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` |
1235	| `U+00DF` LATIN SMALL LETTER SHARP S | `U+00DF` — unchanged | `U+00DF` | `U+0073 U+0073` |
1236	
1237	So `fold` is **not** `Simple_Lowercase_Mapping` (it expands, and it is position-dependent) and
1238	**not** `Case_Folding` (sharp s is unchanged). It is **non-tailored** — the root locale, with no
1239	Turkish/Azeri dotless-i and no Lithuanian tailoring — so the result must never depend on an ambient
1240	locale, an environment variable or a host language setting.
1241	
1242	**Version custody, and the portability consequence it does not hide.** The result of a default case
1243	conversion is determined by the Unicode case data the host carries, so `fold` is deterministic
1244	**given a case-data version**, and this design binds the reference derivation to one:
1245	`native_evidence_model.v2.UNICODE_CASE_DATA_VERSION`, currently **UCD 15.0.0**, the version the
1246	table above was measured against. Two hosts on different case data can fold the same name
1247	differently — for a code point unassigned in one of them (an unassigned code point folds to itself),
1248	or for one whose mapping changed between the versions — and because `libSelection` enters the
1249	context descriptor and therefore `PlanId`, that would be an admission divergence, not a cosmetic
1250	one. This contract does **not** claim the fold is invariant across every runtime. It requires the
1251	version to be a declared, checkable property rather than whatever the runtime happens to ship:
1252	`unicode_case_data_agreement()` reports the running version against the declared one so drift is
1253	disclosed instead of silently changing an outcome. Nothing here narrows the field to ASCII to
1254	sidestep the question — it is simply true that every `lib` name in the pinned compiler's own option
1255	vocabulary is ASCII, where all three operations above coincide, and that is a fact about the current
1256	vocabulary rather than a constraint on the value.
1257	
1258	**Custody: the two arrays answer different questions.** `libSelection` is the
1259	*configuration-facing* record of what the resolved options selected, and it is
1260	what the universe/config agreement is checked against.
1261	`standardLibraryComponentDigests` is the *tree-facing* **complete** declaration
1262	inventory of the retained stdlib closure — one row per `.d.ts` member with its
1263	raw digest, selected or not. So the selection never narrows the inventory and the
1264	inventory never adds a selected name: a missing inventory row refuses
1265	`native.native-context-stdlib-inventory-incomplete:<basename>`, and a tree in
1266	which two paths share a basename refuses
1267	`native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<basename>` — the mapping's
1268	target would not be unique, and an arbitrary resolution is exactly what this
1269	refusal exists to prevent. The join reads **no other input**: not a
1270	caller-supplied map, not a filesystem lookup, not a compiler query, not the
1271	`typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` value on its own.
1272	
1273	**No platform *field*, and the identity is still platform-specific.** Unlike the Rust context there
1274	is no `targetTriple`/`hostTriple`, because TypeScript *resolution semantics* — which specifiers
1275	resolve, which subjects are examined, what is checked — are platform-invariant by design (§1.1).
1276	That is a design selection of this contract, not a measurement, and it is **not** a claim that the
1277	identity is platform-invariant: `toolClosure.closureId` names a signed closure whose foundation
1278	`closure` descriptor includes `platform`, so the same source analysed with the platform-specific
1279	executables of two families mints two `nativeContextId`s — as it must, because different bytes ran
1280	(`typescript-context-identity-is-platform-specific-through-its-signed-tool-closure`).
1281	
1282	**Universe and Plan binding.** `typescript-v2.nativeContextId` is
1283	`H("native.context.typescript.v2", descriptor)` in the `Sha256Text` form. `PlanId` binds the
1284	same digest through `plan.nativeContextDigests`, which takes the **bare 64 hex** (§11, the
1285	foundation `plan` record's spelling) and is a canonical **set**: several units of one language
1286	legitimately share one context, and identical admitted contexts collapse to one member — that is
1287	deduplication of an identical descriptor, never of two different ones.
1288	
1289	`bind_typescript_universe(universe, admission, context)` refuses a universe whose `nativeContextId`
1290	this host did not mint (`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch`) and refuses a Rust-minted context
1291	outright (`native.native-context-language-mismatch`). The **retained context bytes are a required
1292	argument**: there is no context-free admit path, because an optional field-agreement check is not a
1293	rule — a caller that omitted it would obtain exactly the bypass this join exists to close. Omission
1294	is the typed refusal `native.universe-context-not-supplied`
1295	(`typescript-universe-bound-without-the-retained-context-refuses`); context bytes that do not hash to
1296	the admitted id refuse
1297	`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch:context-bytes-are-not-the-admitted-ones`.
1298	
1299	Given those bytes the two records must **agree where they overlap**: a matching `nativeContextId`
1300	commits to the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them, so `languageMode`,
1301	`packageModuleType`, `allowJs`, `checkJs`, `lockfileKind`, `nodeModulesInReadSet`,
1302	`jsDiagnosticsEnabled`, `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `configOrigin`, the `extends`-graph emptiness and the
1303	synthesized-options presence are each checked against the context and refuse
1304	`native.universe-context-field-mismatch:<field>`.
1305	
1306	The context itself also has mandatory agreement rules. `moduleResolutionMode`
1307	equals `configProjection.honoredOptions.moduleResolution`. `libSelection` is
1308	strictly sorted by UTF-8 name bytes, contains no duplicate names under the
1309	published `fold`, and selects the same folded name set as the honored `lib` list
1310	— the same `fold` the component join above uses, and the only one this section
1311	defines; each record retains its specified order for hashing. The closed resolved context
1312	always materializes that nonempty list. When source configuration omits `lib`,
1313	the resolver supplies the pinned compiler's target-default library selection
1314	in both records; `null` is not an alternate resolved spelling.
1315	`standardLibraryComponentDigests`
1316	has strictly unique component keys in UTF-8 order. Context admission refuses any
1317	contradiction before its digest may enter Plan. In synthesized mode every value
1318	in `synthesizedOptions` equals the corresponding honored option, and an absent
1319	optional `jsx` means honored `jsx` is null. Presence alone is insufficient.
1320	These are semantic agreement checks in addition to closed schema validation;
1321	internal diagnostic suffixes remain operational refusal evidence, not new public
1322	DomainDetail codes.

1324	**Independent derivation (§9.5) applies to TypeScript exactly as to Rust.** The worker
1325	recomputes the context from its own sealed inputs; a differing byte is

1353	
1354	### 3.1 `DependencySourceSetV1`
1355	
1356	Identity domain `native.dependency-source-set.v1`. Closed descriptor:
1357	`{schemaVersion:1, language:"rust", lockfileIdentity, packages:
1358	[DependencyPackageSourceV1…] sorted by (name, version, sourceId) UTF-8 bytes,
1359	completeness:{state, missing[]}}`.
1360	
1361	`DependencyPackageSourceV1`:
1362	
1363	| Field | Rule |
1364	|---|---|
1365	| `name`, `version` | exact `[[package]]` values from `Cargo.lock` |
1366	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |
1367	| `sourceId` | exact `source` string from `Cargo.lock`, or `""` for path packages |
1368	| `lockChecksum` | 64-hex from the lock `checksum`, or `null` for git/path |
1369	| `fileManifestSha256` | H(`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, sorted `[{path, contentSha256, byteLength}]`) |
1370	| `fileCount`, `totalBytes` | exact uint64 |
1371	| `acquisition` | `{mode: in-snapshot-path \| in-snapshot-vendored \| imported-descriptor, descriptorId: ImportId\|null, vendorPath\|null}` |
1372	| `checksumVerification` | `tarball-matched \| self-consistent \| not-applicable \| mismatch` — `mismatch` refuses the whole set |
1373	| `provenanceAssurance` | `registry-authenticated \| declared` |
1374	
1375	Verification rules (feedback 3 corrected):
1376	
1377	- **DS-1 (registry, vendored tree)** A vendored directory carries a self-asserted
1378	  `.cargo-checksum.json`. Its `package` field equalling `lockChecksum` proves
1379	  nothing about the files: an attacker rewrites file contents and every `files`
1380	  entry while preserving `package`. The host therefore checks internal
1381	  consistency only (`package == lockChecksum`, every listed file's SHA-256
1382	  matches, no extra or missing files) and records `checksumVerification =

1582	## 4. Resolution completeness (AR-12)
1583	
1584	### 4.1 Two different completeness claims
1585	
1586	A Coverage entry commits two things that were previously conflated:
1587	
1588	1. **Examined universe** — the exhaustive examined subject/target partition
1589	   (`subjectScopeCommitment`, retained). "Did we look at every subject?"
1590	2. **Resolution completeness** — whether every reference/import/call edge
1591	   originating in the examined subjects was resolved to a binding at the requested
1592	   rung, *after resolution was actually attempted over the whole partition*.
1593	   "Could we see every consumer?"
1594	
1595	### 4.1a Producing recipe for `subjectScopeCommitment` (closed)
1596	
1597	The retained C-2 selector deferred computation and verification. This is the successor
1598	recipe; nothing about the historical artifact changes.
1599	
1600	**Recipe.** `subjectScopeCommitment` is the foundation **subject-scope** identity of the
1601	examined partition, re-spelled in the native `Sha256Text` text form:
1602	
1603	```
1604	scope2      = identity-and-evidence H("subject-scope", D)          -> "scope2:"  + hex
1605	commitment  = "sha256:" + the same 64 hex                          -> Sha256Text
1606	```
1607	
1608	where `D` is the closed foundation record
1609	`identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/subject-scope`
1610	`{schemaVersion: 2, snapshotId, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse, relation, resolution,
1611	enumeratorClosure, subjects}`.
1612	
1613	**Inputs, exactly, and where each comes from.** `snapshotId` is the admitted `snapshot2`.
1614	`relation`/`resolution` are the Coverage key's own relation and rung. `sourceUniverse` and
1615	`targetUniverse` are the bare 64-hex universe digests of the same key (§2, §11).
1616	`enumeratorClosure` is the `closure2` of the Plan-bound enumerator that produced the
1617	partition. `subjects` is the **complete** examined subject inventory that enumerator
1618	enumerated over that snapshot, a canonical set (foundation ordering, duplicates refuse
1619	rather than dedupe). **Encoding**: the foundation canonical encoder and `H` frame, imported,
1620	not restated. There is **no native `H` domain for this field**: one preimage, one digest,
1621	two admitted textual spellings (§11).
1622	
1623	**Join with `scope2`.** The commitment is the *identical* digest to the `scope2` the host
1624	binds into the `coverage2` descriptor (`coverage.scopeId`). It is therefore not a second
1625	commitment and cannot drift from the scope it names. Its purpose is that the Coverage
1626	*payload* — the bytes whose `payloadDigest` mints `coverage2` — carries the provider's
1627	in-band commitment to the partition it claims to have examined, which the host then checks
1628	against a value the provider never supplied.
1629	
1630	**Where it is produced and checked (`admit_coverage_result_v3`, the admitted native producer
1631	boundary).** For every `CoverageResultV3` a provider sends, before any `coverage2` exists:
1632	
1633	1. The host builds `D` from **its own** enumeration and mints `scope2`. A provider-supplied
1634	   commitment is never an input to this step.
1635	2. `key.relation`, `key.resolution`, `key.sourceUniverse`, `key.targetUniverse` must equal
1636	   `D`'s (`native.coverage-key-scope-mismatch:<field>`).
1637	3. `key.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the computed commitment
1638	   (`native.subject-scope-commitment-mismatch`).
1639	4. `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the key's
1640	   (`native.examined-universe-commitment-mismatch`) and
1641	   `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectCount` must equal `len(D.subjects)`
1642	   (`native.examined-universe-subject-count-mismatch`). A provider that examined a narrower
1643	   partition than the host enumerated is detected here, and by nothing else.
1644	5. RC-2 (§4.3) is rechecked over the same partition.
1645	6. Only then is `coverage2` minted from `{schemaVersion: 2, scopeId, payloadSchemaDigest,
1646	   payloadDigest}`. `payloadSchemaDigest` is the raw SHA-256 of the **exact registered schema
1647	   DOCUMENT bytes** (§7.2). A caller may restate it but never choose it: a value that is not the
1648	   registered document's digest refuses `native.coverage-payload-schema-not-registered`
1649	   (`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`).
1650	
1651	Every refusal above is `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` (`operational-failed` 4) under the §10
1652	fault law: a worker that lies about its partition contributes no facts, no Coverage and no
1653	Run. This is not a Coverage deficiency; an admitted-but-incomplete input is (§10).
1654	
1655	**Coverage use (`coverage_view_use`).** A `view2` may name a `coverage2` only if that
1656	`coverage2` was admitted at the boundary above and its `scope2` is one of the view's own
1657	`scopeIds`. A hash-valid `coverage2` whose subject scope sits outside the evaluated view is
1658	refused exactly as hidden finding evidence is (identity §3), rather than joined silently.
1659	
1660	**No circularity.** `D` names the snapshot, the universes and the enumerator closure. A
1661	universe descriptor (§2) names its native context, tools and config projection; a native
1662	context names closures; none of them names a scope, a Coverage, a view, an evidence record
1663	or a Run. The derivation order is therefore total and acyclic: closures → native context →
1664	universe → `scope2` → commitment → Coverage payload → `coverage2` → `view2`. The foundation
1665	scope *descriptor* whose raw digest is `scopeDigest` (§1.4, workspace roots and path
1666	prefixes) is a different record with a different job and is not this commitment.
1667	
1668	Cases: `subject-scope-commitment-is-the-scope2-identity-in-native-sha256-text-form`,

1950	### 4.6 Sufficiency v2 (replaces `$.sufficiency`)
1951	
1952	Evaluated in this order; every applicable cause is collected and the most specific
1953	by §10 precedence is reported. `satisfied=true` may carry `disclosures`.
1954	
1955	1. Relation absent from the view → `required-relation-missing`.
1956	2. Rung below `minResolution` → the rung-unavailable cause (`language-tier-unsupported`, `provider-unavailable`, `input-closure-incomplete`, `budget-exhausted`) else `required-relation-missing`.
1957	3. `confidenceMillionths < minConfidenceMillionths` → `confidence-floor-unmet`.
1958	4. Relation `types` with `derivationPolicy=declared-only` and any `compiler-inferred` derivation in the view → `derivation-policy-unmet`.
1959	5. `completeness=complete` and `coverage≠complete` → the entry's own deficiency.
1960	6. `quantifier=universal-negative`: state `partial` or `not-attempted` → `resolution-incomplete` regardless of policy; state `incomplete` or target affected by a dynamic edge → `forbid`: `resolution-incomplete`; `disclose`: disclosure `{unresolved-edges, count, classes}`.
1961	7. `quantifier=universal-negative`, target exported and `exportsClosed≠closed` → `forbid`: `external-consumers-unknown`; `assume-closed`: disclosure.
1962	8. Dependencies (`dependsOn`) recursively (depth ≤ 4) with `partial-ok` for existential requirements and the parent's quantifier/policies for universal negatives.
1963	
1964	There is no early exit. A one-rung relation under `existential` with
1965	`partial-ok` passes step 5 vacuously but still runs steps 1–4 and 8: the former
1966	step 9 shortcut ("satisfied outright") returned before the confidence floor and
1967	let confidence 100000 pass a floor of 900000; it was removed (post-reset
1968	SHOULD-4) and the regression case
1969	`sufficiency-v2-confidence-floor-precedes-one-rung-existential-shortcut`
1970	checks that v2 and the retained v1 oracle both yield `confidence-floor-unmet`
1971	for `clones` at 100000 under floor 900000, and `satisfied` at 1000000.
1972	
1973	**Where a per-requirement outcome travels, and in which vocabulary.** The full
1974	result of `sufficiency_v2` is `{satisfied, deficiency?, disclosures, causes}`:
1975	`causes` is returned on **both** branches — empty when satisfied — and
1976	`disclosures` may be non-empty on the **failing** branch as well as the satisfied
1977	one. What a consumer record carries is the **satisfaction/deficiency projection**
1978	of that result: `satisfied`, and exactly one `DeficiencyV2` member when it is
1979	false, chosen by the §10 precedence over every applicable cause. `causes` and
1980	`disclosures` are **not** projected. They are the producer's own result
1981	arrays and are fields of no retained record — not of `CoverageResultV3`, and
1982	some could not be, since the confidence floor lives in `RequirementV2` and
1983	`required-relation-missing` has no Coverage entry at all. What *is* retained is
1984	the **evidence the evaluation read**: the `coverage2` record with its own
1985	deficiency and `nativeCause` carrier (§10), and the rest of the Run's closure. So
1986	the projection drops nothing that was retained, and re-deriving the full result
1987	means re-running the evaluation over that evidence rather than reading a stored
1988	field. The projection is
1989	total in the only sense a consumer needs: a failing requirement always has exactly
1990	one reported outcome, so omitting the value is never lawful.
1991	
1992	That projected value is a `DeficiencyV2` member and **never** `D9Deficiency`: four
1993	of these nine — `derivation-policy-unmet`, `external-consumers-unknown`,
1994	`input-closure-incomplete`, `resolution-incomplete` — have no `D9Deficiency`
1995	member at all, and the D9-mapped value for all four is the same
1996	`verdict-indeterminate`, so a D9-typed per-requirement field could only be
1997	schema-invalid for four outcomes in nine, collapse those four into one, or drop
1998	the disclosure. The current consumer is
1999	`repair.schema.json#/$defs/EvidenceRequirement.deficiency` (workflows §6), which
2000	names this vocabulary through the drift-checked mirror
2001	`workflows:common#/$defs/NativeSufficiencyDeficiency` and is **required exactly

2003	published in
2004	`native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry/perRequirementConsumerBoundary`.

2037	### 4.8 Type derivation provenance (feedback 12)
2038	
2039	The v1 draft capped JSDoc-free JavaScript type facts at `confidenceMillionths ≤
2040	900000`. That number had no evidence rationale: a compiler-inferred type is exact
2041	under the admitted universe, and JSDoc presence is not a calibrated probability.
2042	Replacement: every `types@checked` fact carries `TypeDerivationV1` =
2043	`{derivationKind: annotated|jsdoc-declared|compiler-inferred, confidenceMillionths:
2044	1000000, confidenceMethod: "native.confidence.v1", checkJs, limitations}`.
2045	`native.confidence.v1` is the versioned, conformance-bound method
2046	"declared-exact: every admitted checked fact is 1000000 under its universe; no
2047	value below 1000000 is produced by a native provider". Rule authors express
2048	"declared types only" through `derivationPolicy=declared-only` (§4.2), which
2049	yields the typed `derivation-policy-unmet` deficiency, not a fake percentage.
2050	`checkJs` is recorded because it changes diagnostics, not derivation.
2051	
2052	**The two clauses have different scopes, and the second is deliberately the wider
2053	one.** The first names the method of `TypeDerivationV1`, whose
2054	`confidenceMillionths` is a schema **constant** `1000000` and whose
2055	`confidenceMethod` is the constant `native.confidence.v1`: that record exists only
2056	on a `types@checked` fact. The second — *no value below 1000000 is produced by a
2057	native provider* — is **not** narrowed to `types@checked`. It is a **provider
2058	emission law** over this whole bundle: no native provider of any relation emits a
2059	confidence below 1000000, because a native fact is exact under its admitted
2060	universe and this design publishes no calibrated probability for any relation. It
2061	is not read as types-scoped, and reading it that way would be a *weakening* — it
2062	would permit a native `clones` or `references` provider to emit a fabricated
2063	percentage, which is exactly what §4.8 removed.
2064	
2065	That leaves `ViewEntryV3.confidenceMillionths`, whose domain is the full integer
2066	range 0…1000000 and which carries **no** `confidenceMethod`. The wider domain is
2067	deliberate and is what keeps §4.6 step 3 reachable: the floor comparison is the
2068	sufficiency evaluation's, it runs for **every** relation, and it must still decide
2069	correctly against an entry a conforming native provider would never have emitted —
2070	a defective or non-conforming provider, and the defensive fixture below. No
2071	*imported* route is offered as an example and none is implied: imported evidence
2072	is a separate plane that mints no `ViewEntryV3` at all (§7, workflows §4), so it
2073	could not supply one of these values, and inventing such a path to explain the
2074	wider domain would be fabricating a mechanism. The named regression case
2075	`sufficiency-v2-confidence-floor-precedes-one-rung-existential-shortcut` is
2076	exactly that: a hand-built evaluator input, **not** a `ViewEntryV3` and **not**
2077	provider emission, exercising `clones` at 100000 against a floor of 900000 so that
2078	the removed early exit cannot come back. Its 100000 is therefore no counterexample
2079	to the emission law and is not evidence that any native provider emits such a
2080	value; it is a defensive fixture for the evaluator, and this contract makes no
2081	claim that the product emits it.

2113	to analyze; OpenSIP does not vouch for it and does not confine it unless a
2114	platform primitive is enforced. The security owner supplies the revocation clock

2117	### 5.2 `AuthorizedExecutionV2`
2118	
2119	Domain `native.authorized-execution.v2`. Closed descriptor bound into
2120	`rust-v2.executionCapableResolution` via `preparedOutputSetId`: `{schemaVersion:2,
2121	operation:"native.prepare", principalClass:"repository-code", projectId,
2122	snapshotId (snapshot2), dependencySourceSetId, toolchain, toolClosure, cfgSetId,
2123	owners: [{ownerKey, kind: build-script|proc-macro, ownerFileManifestSha256,
2124	provenanceAssurance: registry-authenticated|declared|in-snapshot}], effects:
2125	{subprocess, filesystemWrite, network, environment: {requested, enforcement}},
2126	authorization: {mode: interactive-explicit|policy-record, policyRecordId|null, ci},
2127	liveBoundaries: {revocationCheck: before-each-owner, cancellation:
2128	process-group-kill, trustClockRequired: true}, bounds}`.
2129	
2130	`EnforcementV1` values are **copied from the security owner's platform truth
2131	table**; this contract never asserts an `ENFORCED-PLATFORM` value itself, and the
2132	model refuses a record that claims more than the pinned table (`permission-truth-tables.v9.json`:
2133	`network`/`subprocess`/`filesystemWrite` `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`; `environment`
2134	`ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION`).
2135	
2136	**Which token each effect name is copied from (CB4-ADV-3).** The four effect
2137	names here are `effects` field names; the pinned table is over seven closed
2138	permission **tokens**, and the correspondence was determinate by elimination but
2139	published nowhere, so an implementer had to infer it. It is stated:
2140	
2141	| `effects` field | Permission token | `ENFORCED` in v9 (child-process) | What the value means |
2142	|---|---|---|---|
2143	| `subprocess` | `PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED` | `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` | No mechanism prevents the effect; the record states what was asked and answered. |
2144	| `filesystemWrite` | `PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE` | `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` | Same. See the scope note below. |
2145	| `network` | `PT-NET-EGRESS` | `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` | Same. |
2146	| `environment` | `PT-ENV-READ` | `ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION` | The child's environment is constructed by the host, so the capability is never conferred *in this execution mode*. |
2147	
2148	Three scope facts travel with that table and none of them may be dropped:
2149	
2150	1. **The values are per execution mode.** `native.prepare` runs owners as child
2151	   processes, so the `child-process` column is the applicable one. In v9's
2152	   `in-host-process` mode *every* token including `PT-ENV-READ` is
2153	   `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`, because a component sharing the host's address space shares
2154	   its environment. Quoting `ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION` without its mode would
2155	   over-claim.
2156	2. **`PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE` is not repository filesystem authority.** The token
2157	   names the *host's own state store*. Neither it nor any grant over it confers
2158	   authority over the repository tree, and its `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` value says
2159	   precisely that nothing prevents writes anywhere: the executing code holds the
2160	   invoking user's ambient authority throughout. `filesystemWrite` here is a
2161	   disclosure of that fact, never a scoping of it.
2162	3. **`PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED` is deliberately unprojected.** It is the one token
2163	   whose v9 value is `ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER`, and no `effects` field carries
2164	   it, because repository code under `native.prepare` is not routed through a
2165	   host broker. `EnforcementV1` admits the value, so the vocabulary is not
2166	   narrowed; nothing in this contract claims it. The two read-only tokens
2167	   (`PT-FS-READ-PROJECT`, `PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT`) are likewise unprojected: they
2168	   are not effects this record authorizes.
2169	
2170	Confinement is never claimed, and every value above remains the security owner's
2171	to change: if a primitive is later measured on a platform, only that cell moves.
2172	
2173	The mandatory pre-execution sentence, in human and
2174	JSON output: "Build scripts and procedural macros from N packages will run with
2175	your user's authority. OpenSIP does not prevent network access or other effects on
2176	this platform." followed, when applicable, by "Packages with declared
2177	(unauthenticated) provenance: …".
2178	
2179	Authorization: interactive → explicit per-invocation confirmation naming the
2180	owners; CI (`ci=true`) → never prompts; requires a pre-existing `policy-record`
2181	bound to the same `dependencySourceSetId` and toolchain, else
2182	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `native.execution-not-authorized`. Missing live
2183	boundaries, an unavailable bundled linker, or an over-claimed enforcement value
2184	refuse the same way. Authorization is never inherited by another ProjectId,
2185	snapshot with a different owner manifest, or toolchain.

2187	### 5.3 What the preparation step does (feedback 4)
2188	
2189	Owned by the host resolved-inputs adapter (never the semantic worker), after
2190	snapshot seal and dependency-source admission, before PlanId:
2191	
2192	1. Verify the carrier (§3.3 CC-1..CC-5); materialize snapshot and dependency
2193	   sources read-only in private scratch; write the single projected
2194	   `.cargo/config.toml`; construct the environment.
2195	2. Check current trust and revocation state (security owner's clock), then for
2196	   each owner in order: re-check revocation (`before-each-owner`), run the bundled
2197	   Cargo to compile and execute the build script or to build the proc-macro crate
2198	   for the selected cfg set (`cargo check --offline --frozen --locked --target
2199	   <triple>` restricted to the owners; the linker used is the closure linker;
2200	   nothing is installed).
2201	3. **Inside this same authorized step**, drive the bundled compiler's expansion
2202	   through the closure proc-macro server for every invocation site in the
2203	   workspace and dependency crates that names one of the built proc-macro crates,
2204	   and capture the expanded token text per site as `macro-expansion` rows; capture
2205	   `cargo:` directive output as `build-script-directives` rows. Loading the
2206	   proc-macro dylib *is* executing repository code; it happens here, under the
2207	   principal, with the live boundaries, and nowhere else.
2208	4. **Capture required generated data, discard executable products** (R2). For
2209	   each build-script owner: capture the `cargo:` directive lines as a
2210	   `build-script-directives` row; capture as `generated-file` rows the regular
2211	   data files under `OUT_DIR` named by the crate's
2212	   `include!/include_str!/include_bytes!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), …))` sites when
2213	   those are statically determinable, else every regular data file under
2214	   `OUT_DIR` within the PO-4 bounds; discard the build-script binary, every
2215	   dylib/object/archive/executable product and unreferenced scratch files; discard
2216	   the proc-macro dylibs. Referenced paths the script did not produce are recorded
2217	   (`missingReferencedPaths`) and become typed unknowns at analysis. Nothing of
2218	   `OUT_DIR` survives except the captured data rows
2219	   (`preparation-capture-keeps-referenced-data-discards-executable-products`).
2220	   The result is `PreparedOutputSetV3` (`kind: authorized-execution`).
2221	
2222	The semantic worker then consumes the inert set through the protocol
2223	(`PreparedOutputManifest/Chunk/Seal`), looks up expansions by exact site key, and
2224	executes nothing. `RepositoryResolutionV3.workerExecutesRepositoryCode` is the
2225	constant `false`. An external preparer may supply the same inert shape
2226	(`kind: imported-descriptor`, `declared` provenance, §3.6 PO-3); it can never
2227	supply a dylib.

2229	### 5.4 Failure, retry, cancellation, recovery
2230	
2231	| Event | Outcome |
2232	|---|---|
2233	| Owner build script exits non-zero | row `failed`; other owners continue; owner analyzed non-prepared |
2234	| Revocation observed before an owner | step stops; no further owner runs; rows already captured are discarded; `request-rejected` (`native.execution-not-authorized`) |
2235	| Wall or byte bound exceeded | whole step `operational-failed` (4); no row admitted. Existing `HOST.IO_FAILURE` with detail `native.prepare-bound-exceeded`. Not `BudgetExhausted`: a preparation bound is a safety bound of the adapter |
2236	| Cancellation | kill the process group, discard partial OUT_DIR and captured rows, `interrupted` (130) |
2237	| Retry | idempotent by `(dependencySourceSetId, toolchainDigest, cfgSetId, owners manifest)`; an identical inert set already in custody is reused without re-execution and without re-prompt when a policy record covers it |
2238	| Host crash mid-step | scratch reclaimed by ordinary crash reconciliation; no partial set is visible to Plan construction |
2239	| Ambient Cargo config found | `operational-failed` (4), `native.ambient-cargo-config`; never merged |
2240	| Imported set replaces in-host preparation | allowed; PO-0/PO-1/PO-3 apply |

2267	
2268	`minOccurrences 2`; `minBodyBytes 64` (exact); `minTokens 20` (L1–L3,
2269	cross-tsjs); `minTokens 50` (near); `nearThreshold 800000` millionths;

2272	### 6.3 Bodies and language-specific exclusions
2273	
2274	Body spans are function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies.
2275	**Import exclusion means candidate exclusion, not byte editing** (R5): a span that
2276	consists solely of import/`use`/`extern crate`/top-level `require` declarations,
2277	module/file headers, shebangs, license headers, `#![...]` inner attributes or
2278	`declare`-only TypeScript declarations is an *import-only body* and is excluded
2279	as a clone candidate in every mode. A body that is kept is hashed over its
2280	**exact verbatim bytes**: an internal `use`, `import()`, `require` or directive
2281	inside a function body is part of the preimage and is never stripped, rewritten
2282	or normalized away at L0 (`clone-import-only-body-excluded-and-kept-bodies-hash-verbatim`:
2283	two bodies differing only by an internal `use` line are not exact clones).
2284	
2285	| Language | Kept significant at every level | L2 removes | L3 renames |
2286	|---|---|---|---|
2287	| TypeScript/JavaScript | string/template literal contents, regex literals, JSX text, `'use strict'`/`'use client'` directives, `/// <reference>` and `// @ts-*` directives, decorators | non-directive comments | local `let/const/var`, parameters, local function names, destructured locals; **not** properties, imports, exports, globals, `this` members |
2288	| Rust | macro invocation token trees verbatim, attributes including `#[cfg]`, string/byte/raw literals, lifetimes | non-doc comments | local `let` bindings, parameters, closure parameters, pattern bindings; **not** fields, paths, generics, trait names, macro-introduced names |
2289	
2290	Fact identity is same-language: `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` is
2291	in the preimage, so a TypeScript body never groups with a JavaScript or Rust body
2292	in `exact`/`normalized`/`structural`, even with identical bytes.
2293	
2294	### 6.4 TS/JS cross-language decision (feedback 9)
2295	
2296	Decision: `languageId` **stays** in exact fact identities (a `.ts` and a `.js`
2297	body are different facts). Cross-TS/JS matching is a separate **candidate-only**
2298	mode `cross-tsjs` under the named deterministic syntax projection
2299	`tsjs-erasure-v1`:
2300	
2301	- Removed before L3 normalization: type annotations, `type`/`interface`
2302	  declarations, type parameter lists, `as` assertions, `satisfies`, non-null `!`,
2303	  definite-assignment `!`, `declare`/`readonly`/`abstract`/access modifiers,
2304	  `implements` clauses, `import type`/`export type`.
2305	- **Never removed**: tokens that TypeScript compiles into runtime behavior —
2306	  `enum`/`const enum`, parameter properties (`constructor(private x)`),
2307	  value-bearing `namespace`, decorators, `import =`. A body containing any of them
2308	  is **excluded** from cross matching with reason

2310	- Output rows carry `projectionId=tsjs-erasure-v1`, `authority=candidate-only`,
2311	  `semanticEquivalenceClaimed=false`, `automaticDeletionEligible=false` as schema
2312	  constants. A cross candidate is never a baseline member, never a Control input,
2313	  never a repair prerequisite.

2315	Cases: `clone-cross-tsjs-candidate-only`, `clone-cross-tsjs-runtime-significant-excluded`.

2464	## 9. Provider protocol successors (wire)
2465	
2466	### 9.1 Versions and identity negotiation (feedback 1)
2467	
2468	`rust-semantic` protocol major **3**; `typescript-semantic` protocol major **2**.
2469	Capability tokens (closed, `CapabilityToken`): identity tokens
2470	`source-identity-snapshot2`, `plan-identity-plan2`, `fact-identity-fact2`,
2471	`coverage-v3`; plus `sealed-vfs-v1`, `multi-stage-analyze-v1`,
2472	`<lang>-semantic-facts-v1`, `resolution-completeness-v2`, `unresolved-edge-v1`,
2473	`dependency-source-v1` (Rust), `prepared-output-v3` (Rust), `native-context-v2`.
2474	`HelloV3` also carries `identityVersions: {snapshot:2, plan:2, fact:2, coverage:3}`
2475	and `HelloAckV3` must echo it exactly.
2476	
2477	Reject-before-disclosure ordering:
2478	
2479	1. **Plan time (no spawn).** The host reads the signed capability row. The four
2480	   identity tokens are required for every worker; a row lacking any of them, or
2481	   any token the Plan needs, is never spawned: affected Coverage keys are
2482	   `unknown / provider-unavailable` (cause `capability-missing`). No raw
2483	   `snapshot2`, `plan2` or source byte reaches a worker that cannot name them
2484	   (`negotiation-v1-only-worker-never-spawned`).
2485	2. **Hello → HelloAck (no source bytes).** Exact recursive equality of the token
2486	   array and identity versions; mismatch → `FAULT`, `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`,

2854	The encoding is normative, and its **units** are stated because they differ
2855	between the two operations. Let `raw` be the composed subject
2856	`<registered key>[:<value>]` as an **admitted Unicode scalar string**. Length and
2857	slicing count **Unicode code points**, which is what `BoundedText`'s JSON Schema
2858	`maxLength` counts — not UTF-8 bytes and not UTF-16 code units. If
2859	`len(raw) ≤ 1024` the subject **is** `raw`. Otherwise it is
2860	
2861	```
2862	raw[: 1024 − len("...#sha256:") − 64] + "...#sha256:" + hex(SHA256(raw.encode("utf-8")))
2863	```
2864	
2865	— the marker `...#sha256:` is ASCII, the digest is exactly 64 lowercase hex
2866	characters, the SHA-256 input is exactly `raw` encoded as UTF-8 with **no**
2867	additional normalization, and the result is exactly 1024 code points. A
2868	non-ASCII value therefore has a UTF-8 byte length that may exceed 1024 while its
2869	scalar length does not, and the two operations must not be conflated.

2872	collision-resistance assumption** for SHA-256; this is not a claim that collision
2873	is impossible. **The guarantee is confined to what is published** — the bounded
2874	subject and its digest. This contract does **not** promise a separate retained
2875	store of the untruncated value and names none; a host that keeps its own
2876	operational log may match it by recomputing this digest, which is why the digest

3135	that is the dialect, never the map: a body identity that varied with unrelated
3136	crates would be neither meaningful nor representable. When the map's distinct
3137	value set has exactly one member — the ordinary case, including a large
3138	single-edition workspace — that member is the dialect of every body and no owner
3139	selection arises. When it has more than one, the **owning compilation unit
3140	decides**.

3142	More precisely, the **compilation target** decides, not the package. Cargo
3143	documents an `edition` on a target that **defaults to** `package.edition` when
3144	absent — `cargo metadata` lists `targets[].edition` and states the package value
3145	is a default individual targets may differ from, and the `[[bin]]`/`[lib]`
3146	`edition` field, though deprecated, is still documented. So *source → package →
3147	package edition* misses a supported override, and a universe whose package
3148	defaults **all agree** can still contain a target that does not. There is
3149	therefore **no single-edition fast path**: a `clones` fact over a Rust universe
3150	requires the committed ownership relation whatever the package map looks like,

3202	**Because the selection is committed inside the record whose `h-identity` the
3203	universe names, a different selection is a different record, a different identity
3204	and therefore a different `sourceUniverse`.** That is what makes the required case
3205	representable: one physical source path compiled by two targets at two editions is

3210	Selection is exact and total, and the order of decision is fixed so each step has
3211	its own cause. No committed ownership refuses. `enumeration: partial` refuses
3212	**before any row is read**. Rows are those whose `path` **equals** the enclosing
3213	fact's anchor path — never a prefix, never a nearest directory, never a first
3214	match — and no row at all refuses as not-compiled. Rows are then restricted to
3215	`selectedUnitIds`, and a path compiled only by **unselected** targets refuses as
3216	not-selected rather than borrowing an out-of-scope edition. Selected owners whose

3226	committed in the identity, so every consumer sees it and it changes the universe.

3228	scope may exist that is not listed and could contradict a listed one — a gap in
3229	knowledge, invisible as a selection, admitting no dialect at all. Silently
3230	omitting a conflicting owner from the table is not a selection either: an
3231	omission leaves no trace, whereas a selection is part of the universe identity.

3240	refuses, which is a real ambiguity in the input rather than a gap in the law.

3431	The **pre-Plan admission order** is published, because it is what makes the typed refusal reachable. A complete `analysis-spec` - defaulted or explicitly supplied - is admitted in three steps: **bounded selection cardinality first**, then generic schema validation of the whole record, then the closed native capability vocabulary. Cardinality precedes schema validation because a `maxItems` breach is reported generically: the exception restates the entire instance and carries no typed scope projection — no public detail, class, exit, `field:count>limit` subject or per-field remedy — even though its own structured fields do identify the failing path and the bound; an oversized ordinary selection is not a malformed record and is not published as one. The first step is **conditional on the field actually being a JSON array in an object**, and nothing is coerced: a missing field, a null, a boolean, a number, a string or an object proceeds untouched to the schema step and refuses there as the malformed record it is. Without that condition a 1025-character string would be published as 1025 capabilities, which is a misclassification and not a scope limit. Everything a schema is genuinely better at - an unknown property, a wrong type, a missing field, a missing `schemaVersion` - still refuses at the schema step exactly as before, **for every input that reaches that step**. Which inputs those are follows from the condition, not from the bound alone: step 1 refuses **only** an actual JSON array that is over its bound, so a spec whose `requestedCapabilities` is **absent, null, a boolean, a number, a string or an object** proceeds untouched to the schema step and refuses there as the malformed record it is, and so does an array **within** its bound that is malformed in any other way. The ordering is exact and cardinality-first, so an input that is *both* an oversized array and otherwise malformed refuses with the cardinality result - `PROJECT.SCOPE_LIMIT`, subject `field:count>limit` - and its schema fault is reported on a later, narrowed request rather than in the same one. Nothing is lost or misclassified by that: the malformed spec is refused either way, no Plan or Run is minted for the refused step, and the refusal that does fire states a true fact about the instance. **The two routes are not, however, the same public termination, and this paragraph does not flatten them.** The cardinality refusal is origin-independent - `request-rejected` (2), `REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE`, `PROJECT.SCOPE_LIMIT` - because an oversized ordinary selection is not malformed. The schema refusal keeps §10's **origin-dependent** routing: an externally supplied or retained spec is `request-rejected` (2) / `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, while a host-generated internal layer minting its own invalid spec is **`operational-failed` (4)** / `SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE` with `faultCause: host-invariant`. Reordering the two steps therefore never converts a host-invariant fault into a request rejection, and never the reverse. One condition is reordered for one shape, and none is added. This order is the **request** boundary only. Validation of a **retained** `analysis-spec` payload at Run closure is a different question with a different answer - an oversized array there means corruption rather than an oversized request - and nothing here changes it: Run closure schema-validates the retained record before any capability vocabulary admission, so an over-long retained array already refuses there.

3433	What this refusal is **not**. It is not a truncation: no capability is dropped, no root is dropped, and the matrix-fixed default and every advertised capability promise are unchanged. It is not a host defect: the host computed the default correctly and the *request* simply cannot be expressed within a published bound, so it is `request-rejected`/`REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE` and never `host-invariant`. 21	left by an EARLIER run can be sitting on disk under the same name. Declining to hash either is
22	the point. `passed` is false.

    The order is the point, and it is published in native section 10:

      1. bounded selection cardinality - ONLY when `requestedCapabilities` is actually a JSON array in an
         object; a valid array over the bound refuses TYPED here, before generic maxItems validation
      2. `validate_foundation("analysis-spec", ...)` - generic schema validation of the whole record
      3. `admit_requested_capabilities` - the closed native vocabulary
      4. `IM.admit_parameter_selection` - the FOUNDATION payload-registry selection law over
         `parameters` (at most one selected parameter per registered row), appended so that steps
         1-3 keep their exact published precedence and no existing route is reclassified

    Step 1 is CONDITIONAL, and that condition is not a detail. An earlier revision indexed the key and took its
    length unconditionally, so a spec missing the field raised KeyError, a null/boolean/integer raised TypeError,
    and a 1025-character STRING was reported as 1025 capabilities with a full typed scope refusal and a
    schema-admitted failure envelope. Every one of those is a malformed record that the schema owns, and one of
    them was publicly misclassified. Nothing is coerced and no shape is repaired: any value that is not an actual
    array simply proceeds to step 2 and refuses there as the malformed record it is.

    Step 1 precedes step 2 for the shape it does own because a `maxItems` breach is reported by jsonschema as a
    generic ValidationError that restates the entire instance - measured at ~265 000 characters for a 1034-row
    spec - without the required typed public scope projection. Its structured fields identify the path and
    bound. An oversized ORDINARY SELECTION is not a malformed record and
    must not be published that way. Everything a schema is genuinely better at - unknown properties, wrong types,
    a missing field, a missing schemaVersion - still refuses at step 2 exactly as before, for every input that
    REACHES step 2. Step 1 refuses ONLY an actual JSON array over its bound, so a missing field, a null, a
    boolean, a number, a string, an object, and an in-bound array malformed some other way all reach step 2
    untouched. The order is exact and cardinality-first, so an input that is BOTH an oversized array and
    otherwise malformed refuses with the cardinality result and reports its schema fault on a later, narrowed
    request; the malformed spec is refused either way and no Plan or Run is minted for the refused step. The two
    routes are NOT the same public termination: the cardinality refusal is origin-independent request-rejected /
    exit 2 (REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE, PROJECT.SCOPE_LIMIT), while the schema refusal keeps section 10's
    ORIGIN-DEPENDENT routing - request-rejected / exit 2 for an externally supplied or retained spec, but
    operational-failed / exit 4 (SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE, faultCause host-invariant) for a host-generated
    internal layer minting its own invalid spec. Reordering never converts one into the other. One condition is
    reordered for one shape; none is added.

    validation - and it is stated as no more than that. It is NOT a claim that the earlier placement was reached

    before the vocabulary helper is invoked, so an oversized retained array refuses as a ValidationError there and
    never arrives. Nothing about retained Run closure changes here.

    WHAT THIS BOUNDARY IS NOT. It is pre-Plan for THIS analysis step, and that is all it scopes: refusing here

    invocation keep their ordinary operational attribution under workflow law, and any earlier step that already
    committed an outcome keeps it. Nothing about retained-payload validation, corruption classification or any
    other admission is changed."""
